en: The Perfection of Wisdom in Twenty-Five Thousand Lines, Chapter IV.
Then the Venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed a non-perfection."
The Blessed One said:
"Subhūti, it is by depending on the non-existence of space.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of equanimity is indeed the perfection of wisdom.
The Blessed One said:
“Because it is based on the equality of the non-apprehension of all phenomena.”
Subhūti said:
"O Bhagavat, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of solitude.
The Bhagavat said:
"By virtue of absolute emptiness.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed an invincible perfection."
The Blessed One said:
"By way of the non-apprehensibility of all phenomena.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is a perfection without a track.
The Blessed One said: “Because it is nameless and bodiless.”
Subhūti said: "O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of space.
The Blessed One said:
"Because inhalation and exhalation are unapprehendable.
Subhūti said: "O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed a perfection that is beyond verbal expression."
The Blessed One said:
"By way of the non-apprehension of applied and sustained thought.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is nameless.
The Blessed One said: “Because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are unapprehendable.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is a perfection of non-going.
The Blessed One said:
"Because all dharmas are characterized by non-coming.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is an unassailable perfection."
The Blessed One said:
"Because all dharmas are ungraspable.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is an inexhaustible perfection.
The Blessed One said:
“Because all phenomena are absolutely exhausted and have been exhausted from the very beginning.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of non-arising is indeed the perfection of wisdom.
The Blessed One said:
"Because all dharmas are characterized by non-arising and non-ceasing.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is a perfection of the non-agent."
The Blessed One said:
"Because of the non-apprehension of an agent.
Subhūti said:
“O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the non-knower.
The Blessed One said:
“Because of the non-apprehension of a knower.”
Subhūti said:
"O Bhagavat, this perfection of wisdom is a perfection of non-transmigration.
The Bhagavat said:
"Because of the non-apprehension of death and rebirth.
Subhūti said: "O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of non-discipline."
The Blessed One said:
"Because all phenomena are by nature unconquerable.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of dream.
The Blessed One said: “Because of the non-apprehensibility of those who see dreams.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed a perfection like an echo.
The Blessed One said:
"Because of the non-apprehensibility of the excellence of sound.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of reflection."
The Blessed One said:
"By way of the non-apprehension of the original object and its reflection.
Subhūti said:
“O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is a perfection of mirages.
The Blessed One said:
“Because of the non-apprehensibility of masses of water.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of illusion.
The Blessed One said:
"Because its causal signs are not perceived.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed a perfection of non-affliction."
The Blessed One said:
"By way of the non-apprehension of the intrinsic nature of the afflictions.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is a non-perfection of purification.
The Blessed One said:
“Because of the non-apprehension of afflicted sentient beings.”
Subhūti said:
"O Bhagavān, this perfection of non-adherence is indeed the perfection of wisdom.
The Bhagavān said:
"Based on the non-apprehension of space.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of non-proliferation."
The Blessed One said:
"On account of the total eradication of all conceptual proliferation.
Subhūti said:
“O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of non-conceptualization.
The Blessed One said:
“Because it effects the total eradication of all conceptualizations.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of immovability.
The Blessed One said:
"It is by taking the abiding in the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) as the basis, Subhūti. Thus [are] the aspects of omniscience.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of dispassion (*virāga*)."
The Blessed One said:
"By way of the non-apprehension of detachment.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is a perfection of non-abiding.
The Blessed One said:
“Because it is based on the non-conceptualization of all phenomena.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is a perfection of peace.
The Blessed One said:
"Because it is the realization of the non-falsity of all dharmas.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed a perfection of non-attachment."
The Blessed One said:
"By way of the non-apprehension of passion.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is a perfection that is without fault.
The Blessed One said: “Because faults are non-existent.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of non-delusion.
The Blessed One said:
"Because it dispels the darkness of delusion.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed a perfection free from afflictions."
The Blessed One said:
"On account of the non-existence of conceptual construction.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the absence of sentient beings.
The Blessed One said:
“Because of the non-apprehension of sentient beings.”
Subhūti said:
"O Bhagavān, this perfection of wisdom is an immeasurable perfection.
The Bhagavān said:
"Because all phenomena do not arise.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection that does not approach either extreme."
The Blessed One said:
"On account of their absolute non-apprehensibility.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the unconfused perfection, because it is the non-confusion of all dharmas.
The Blessed One said:
“Because it is based on the non-confusion of all dharmas.”
Subhūti said:
"This perfection, Blessed One, which is to say the perfection of wisdom, is ungraspable.
The Blessed One said:
This is because it transcends the stage of the śrāvaka and the stage of the pratyekabuddha.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of non-conceptuality."
The Blessed One said:
"By way of non-conceptual non-apprehension.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
The Blessed One said: “Because all phenomena are unapprehendable as being without measure.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed a perfection of non-attachment.
The Blessed One said:
"Because all phenomena have the same nature as space.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of impermanence."
The Blessed One said:
"By virtue of the indestructibility of all phenomena.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of suffering.
The Blessed One said:
“Because it is characterized by the non-attachment to all phenomena.”
Subhūti said: "O Blessed One, this perfection of emptiness is indeed the perfection of wisdom.
The Blessed One said:
"Because it has the sense of being entirely without fruit.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of selflessness."
The Blessed One said:
"Because of the non-attachment to all dharmas.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the signless.
The Blessed One said: “Because all phenomena are devoid of signs.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of internal emptiness.
The Blessed One said:
"Based on the non-apprehension of internal phenomena.
Subhūti said: "O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of external emptiness."
The Blessed One said:
"By way of the non-apprehension of external phenomena.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of internal-and-external emptiness.
The Blessed One said:
“Because of the non-apprehension of internal and external phenomena.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the emptiness of emptiness.
The Blessed One said:
"Based on the non-apprehensibility of emptiness and non-emptiness.
Subhūti said: "O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the great perfection of emptiness."
The Blessed One said:
"By virtue of the non-apprehensibility of great emptiness.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the emptiness of the ultimate truth.
The Blessed One said:
“Because the emptiness of the ultimate truth is non-apprehendable.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the emptiness of the conditioned.
The Blessed One said:
"Because conditioned emptiness is non-apprehensible.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of unconditioned emptiness."
The Blessed One said:
"By way of the non-apprehension of the emptiness of the unconditioned.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of absolute emptiness.
The Blessed One said: “Because absolute emptiness is non-apprehendable.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the emptiness that is without beginning or end.
The Blessed One said:
"By virtue of the non-apprehensibility of the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the emptiness of non-repudiation."
The Blessed One said:
"By way of the non-apprehensibility of the emptiness of non-dispersal.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
The Blessed One said:
“Because the non-apprehension of the emptiness of intrinsic nature is based upon it.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the emptiness of all dharmas.
The Blessed One said:
"By virtue of the non-apprehensibility of all dharmas.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of the emptiness of intrinsic characteristics."
The Blessed One said:
"By way of their being devoid of specific characteristics.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the emptiness of non-apprehension.
The Blessed One said:
“Because of the non-apprehensibility of the three times within the three times.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
The Blessed One said:
"By way of the non-apprehension of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Thus are the aspects of the knowledge of the path.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of the applications of mindfulness."
The Blessed One said:
"By virtue of the non-apprehension of body, feelings, mind, and phenomena.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of right exertion is indeed the perfection of wisdom.
The Blessed One said:
“Because of the non-apprehension of unwholesome and wholesome dharmas.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of the bases of psychic power is indeed the perfection of wisdom.
The Blessed One said:
"Because of the non-apprehensibility of desire, vigor, mind, and investigation.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of the faculties is indeed the perfection of wisdom."
The Blessed One said:
"By way of the non-apprehension of faith and so forth.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of power is indeed the perfection of wisdom.
The Blessed One said:
“Because the five powers are non-apprehendable.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of the factors of enlightenment is indeed the perfection of wisdom.
The Blessed One said:
"By reason of the non-apprehension of the seven factors of enlightenment.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of the path is indeed the perfection of wisdom."
The Blessed One said:
"By way of the non-apprehension of the noble eightfold path.
Thus are the aspects based upon the path to omniscience.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of emptiness.
The Blessed One said:
"Because of the non-apprehension of views.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of the signless."
The Blessed One said:
"On account of the non-apprehension of discursive thoughts.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the wishless.
The Blessed One said:
“Because of the non-apprehension of any aspiration.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of the eight liberations.
The Blessed One said:
"Because of the non-apprehensibility of the eight liberations.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling."
The Blessed One said:
"Because of the non-apprehension of the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the four truths.
The Blessed One said:
“Because of the non-apprehension of the origin and the cessation [of suffering].”
Subhūti said:
"This perfection of giving, Blessed One, is indeed the perfection of wisdom.
The Blessed One said:
"Based on the non-apprehensibility of stinginess.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of ethical discipline."
The Blessed One said:
"On account of the non-apprehensibility of immorality.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of patience is indeed the perfection of wisdom.
The Blessed One said:
“Because of the non-apprehensibility of malice.”
Subhūti said:
"This perfection of wisdom, Blessed One, is the perfection of vigor.
The Blessed One said:
“Because of the non-apprehension of laziness.
Subhūti said: “This perfection of meditation, O Blessed One, is indeed the perfection of wisdom.”
The Blessed One said:
"On account of the non-apprehension of distraction.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of wisdom.
The Blessed One said:
“Because of the non-apprehensibility of faulty wisdom.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of skillful means.
The Blessed One said:
"By way of the non-apprehension of non-expedient means.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of aspiration."
The Blessed One said:
"By way of the non-apprehension of non-vow.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of power.
The Blessed One said:
“Because of the non-apprehension of weakness.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of knowledge.
The Blessed One said:
"Based on the non-apprehension of ignorance.
These are the aspects based upon the knowledge of the paths.
Subhūti said:
“O Blessed One, this perfection of the ten powers is indeed the perfection of wisdom.
The Blessed One said:
“By virtue of the non-apprehensibility of all phenomena.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of fearlessness.
The Blessed One said:
"Because it is based on the non-despondency regarding the knowledge of the paths.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of the analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid)."
The Blessed One said:
"Because of the non-attachment and non-obstruction of all-knowledge.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the unique qualities of a Buddha.
The Blessed One said:
“Because it transcends all dharmas.”
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of suchness.
The Blessed One said:
"Based on the suchness spoken by all Buddhas.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the perfection of the Self-Existent (svayaṃbhū)."
The Blessed One said:
"By virtue of mastery over all dharmas.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed the perfection of the qualities of a Buddha.
The Blessed One said:
“Because it is based on the complete awakening to all phenomena in all their aspects.”
"Thus, these aspects have been described as being based upon the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā). Then, this thought occurred to Śakra, the lord of the gods:
"Those sons of good family and daughters of good family must have performed services for previous Victors."
Those to whom this *prajñāpāramitā* shall come within the range of their hearing will be beings who have planted roots of merit under the Tathāgatas;

those to whom this *prajñāpāramitā* shall come within the range of their hearing will be beings who have been sustained by spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*). How much more so, then, for those who will take it up, preserve it, recite it, master it, and attend to it with wise reflection!
Having taken it up, retained it, recited it, and mastered it, they will practice for the sake of suchness;

those sons of good family and daughters of good family will have attended upon many Buddhas. Those who, having heard this perfection of wisdom, will take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, and attend to it with wise reflection—[they shall do so].
Having taken up, retained, recited, and mastered [this teaching], they will practice for the sake of suchness; furthermore,
those sons of good family and daughters of good family have in the past questioned, interrogated, served, honored, and attended upon the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones.

Those who, having heard this perfection of wisdom, will not be afraid, will not be terrified, and will not fall into terror—these have practiced the perfection of giving under many millions of Buddhas; likewise, they have practiced the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, and the perfection of meditation under many millions of Buddhas; those who, having heard this perfection of wisdom, will not be afraid, will not be terrified, and will not fall into terror, have practiced this perfection of wisdom under many millions of Buddhas.
Then the Venerable Śāriputra said this to the Blessed One:

"Blessed One, those sons of good family or daughters of good family who, having heard this very profound perfection of wisdom, shall not be terrified, shall not be frightened, and shall not fall into terror;
and having heard it, shall take it up, bear it in mind, recite it, master it, and attend to it with wise reflection—"
Those sons of good family or daughters of good family should be regarded as irreversible bodhisattva mahāsattvas. Why is that?

Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is profound. Indeed, it is not possible for one who has not previously practiced the six perfections to have faith in this profound perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Blessed One, those sons of good family or daughters of good family...

They will think that this profound *prajñāpāramitā* is to be rejected; indeed, these sons of good family and daughters of good family have already rejected this profound *prajñāpāramitā* in the past. Why is that?
Because for those sons of good family and daughters of good family, there is no [faith] in this profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

They lacked faith, they lacked clarity, they lacked affection, and they lacked resolute conviction; those sons of good family and daughters of good family had not questioned the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas,
or Śrāvakas as to how one should practice the perfection of generosity.
How should one practice the perfection of ethical discipline?
And how should one practice the perfection of patience?
How should one practice the perfection of vigor?
How should one practice the perfection of meditative concentration? How should one practice the perfection of wisdom?
How should one practice internal emptiness?
How should one practice in the emptiness of the external?
How should one practice in the emptiness of the internal and external?
Up to: how should one practice in the emptiness of the nature of non-existence?
How are the foundations of mindfulness to be cultivated? How the right efforts?
How the bases of psychic power?
What are the faculties? What are the powers?
What are the factors of enlightenment?
How should the noble eightfold path be cultivated?
How should the immeasurables, the meditative absorptions, and the formless attainments be cultivated?
How should the noble truths be cultivated?
How are the eight liberations to be cultivated? How are the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling to be cultivated?
How are emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness to be cultivated?
How should the six superknowledges be cultivated?
How should the meditative concentrations be attained? How should the gateways of the dhāraṇīs be entered?
How are the ten powers of a Tathāgata to be cultivated? How are the grounds of self-confidence to be cultivated?

"How should the analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid) be cultivated? How should the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) be cultivated? Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, said this to the venerable Śāriputra:

"Venerable Śāriputra, the perfection of wisdom is profound. What would be surprising about this? That those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who were not even previously resolved upon this profound perfection of wisdom [would now do so]—regarding the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, and the perfection of meditative concentration."
They lack conviction in the perfection of wisdom;
they lack conviction in internal emptiness, up to and including the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence.
They lack conviction in the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening;
they lack conviction in the immeasurables, the meditative concentrations, and the formless attainments;
and they lack conviction in emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.

They lack conviction in the eight liberations and the nine successive meditative attainments; they lack conviction in the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four grounds of self-confidence, the four analytical knowledges, and the five superknowledges;
they lack conviction in the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. That those who would reject these [teachings] exist is not surprising.

I pay homage to the Blessed Prajñāpāramitā. He who pays homage to the Prajñāpāramitā pays homage to the knowledge of the All-Knowing One. Then the Blessed One said this to Śakra, the lord of the gods:
"So it is, Kauśika, so it is. He who pays homage to the perfection of wisdom pays homage to the knowledge of the omniscient one. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, the omniform knowledge of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, has been brought forth from this."

And it is from the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) that the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is manifested. Kauśika, a son of good family or a daughter of good family who wishes to transcend omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) should abide in the perfection of wisdom.

Likewise, one who wishes to abide in the knowledge of the path (*mārgajñatā*), who wishes to generate the knowledge of all aspects, who wishes to eradicate all afflictions along with their latencies and habitual tendencies (*vāsanā-anuśaya*), who wishes to awaken to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*), and who wishes to turn the wheel of Dharma, should abide in the perfection of wisdom.

A son of good family or a daughter of good family should abide in the perfection of wisdom, if they desire to establish beings in the fruit of stream-entry, if they desire to establish beings in the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, or arhatship; if they desire to establish beings in pratyekabuddha-enlightenment;
or if they desire to establish beings in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
"A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who wishes to lead the community of monks should apply himself to the yoga of the perfection of wisdom.
When this was said, Śakra, lord of the gods, addressed the Blessed One:
"How, Blessed One, does a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva become established in the perfection of wisdom?"
Or how is it appropriate?
How does one become established in the perfection of meditation, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of patience, and the perfection of ethical discipline;
and how does one become established in the perfection of generosity?
Or how does he apply himself to yoga?

Or how, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, does he apply himself to yoga regarding internal emptiness, up to and including the application of yoga regarding the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence?
Lord, how does a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, apply himself to yoga regarding the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment?
In this way, [he practices] in the immeasurables, the dhyānas, and the formless attainments. How does he apply himself to yoga regarding emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness?
In this way, he applies himself to yoga regarding the eight liberations and the nine successive meditative attainments. How does he apply himself to yoga regarding the superknowledges?

In this way, [he practices] regarding the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four grounds of self-confidence, and the four analytical knowledges. How, while coursing in the perfection of wisdom, does he [practice] regarding the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha?
"...do they enter into yoga, O Bodhisattva Mahāsattva? When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to Śakra, the lord of the gods:
"Excellent, excellent, Kauśika! It is indeed excellent of you, Kauśika, that you ask the Tathāgata about this matter."
"You consider it necessary to ask further questions. This inspired eloquence of yours, Kauśika, has also arisen through the power of the Buddha.
Therefore, Kauśika, listen well and attend closely; I shall speak to you. Thus, there are four modes of application:
here, Kauśika, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom does not abide in form.
When one does not abide in form, then one does not apply oneself to form; [likewise] in feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
When one does not abide in consciousness, then one does not apply oneself to consciousness. One does not abide in the eye.
Thus, he does not abide in the ear, the nose, the tongue, the body, or the mind;
in this way, he applies himself to the yoga of the perfection of wisdom. He does not abide in form;
likewise, he does not abide in sound, odor, taste, tangibles, or mental phenomena.
In this way, one applies oneself to the yoga of the perfection of wisdom. One does not abide in eye-consciousness,
one does not abide in eye-contact,
and one does not abide in the feeling conditioned by eye-contact.
In this way, he does not abide in ear, nose, tongue, body, or mental consciousness;
he does not abide in mental contact;
he does not abide in the feeling conditioned by mental contact.
In this way, one applies oneself to the yoga of the perfection of wisdom. One does not abide in the earth element;
likewise, one does not abide in the water element, the fire element, the wind element, the space element, or the consciousness element.
In this way, one applies oneself to the yoga of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). One does not abide in ignorance (*avidyā*);

likewise, one does not abide in formative forces (*saṃskāra*), consciousness (*vijñāna*), name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*), the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), contact (*sparśa*), feeling (*vedanā*), craving (*tṛṣṇā*), grasping (*upādāna*), becoming (*bhava*), birth (*jāti*), nor in old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, depression, and despair (*jarāmaraṇa-śoka-parideva-duḥkha-daurmanasyopāyāsa*).
It is in this way that one applies oneself to the yoga of the perfection of wisdom; one does not abide in the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*).
In this way, one does not abide in morality, patience, vigor, meditation, or the perfection of wisdom;
in this way, one applies oneself to the yoga of the perfection of wisdom. One does not abide in internal emptiness;
in this way, one applies oneself to the yoga of the perfection of wisdom, up to and including not abiding in the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence.
In this way, one applies oneself to the yoga of the perfection of wisdom. One does not abide in the applications of mindfulness;

in this way, one applies oneself to the yoga of the perfection of wisdom. Likewise, one does not abide in the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, or the path;
in this way, one applies oneself to the yoga of the perfection of wisdom. Likewise, in the four immeasurables, the four meditative concentrations, and the four...

He does not abide in the formless attainments, the five superknowledges, emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, the eight liberations, the nine successive meditative attainments, or the gateways of the dhāraṇīs;

in this way, he applies himself to the yoga of the perfection of wisdom. Likewise, he does not abide in the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the grounds of self-confidence, the analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
In this way, one applies oneself to the yoga of the perfection of wisdom. Why is that?
Because he does not perceive form—that wherein he might abide or wherein he might apply himself to yoga—nor feeling, perception, or mental formations.
One does not apprehend consciousness such that it might abide therein or wherein it might apply itself to yoga;
likewise for the elements, the sense bases, the factors of dependent origination, the perfections, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment,
all the emptinesses, all the meditative concentrations, all the doors of dhāraṇī, the immeasurables, the dhyānas, the formless attainments, and the eight liberations.

One does not apprehend the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling, emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, the superknowledges, the ten powers, the four grounds of self-confidence, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, wherein one might abide or to which one might apply oneself in yoga.
This is the practice of non-abiding in form and so forth.

Furthermore, Kauśika, a bodhisattva mahāsattva does not apply himself to form; in that he does not apply himself to form, he thus enters into yoga with respect to form, and likewise with respect to feeling, perception, and mental formations.
It is not applicable to consciousness;

that which is not applicable to consciousness—in this way, one applies oneself to yoga regarding consciousness. Likewise regarding the elements, the sense bases, dependent origination, the perfections, the factors of enlightenment, the emptinesses, the noble truths, the immeasurables, the meditative absorptions, and the formless attainments.

One does not apply oneself to emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, the eight liberations, the nine successive meditative attainments, the superknowledges, all the gateways of concentration and dhāraṇī, the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; that which does not apply itself to the qualities of a Buddha [is non-applying].
In this way, he applies himself to the practice of the Buddha-qualities. Why is that?
Because that bodhisattva mahāsattva does not perceive form from the perspective of the past limit, nor does he perceive form from the perspective of the future limit.
One does not apprehend form in the middle; one does not apprehend feeling, perception, or mental formations; nor does one apprehend consciousness from the past limit.
One does not apprehend consciousness from the perspective of the future limit,
nor does one apprehend consciousness from the perspective of the middle. In this same way, one does not apprehend the elements, the sense bases, the factors of dependent origination, the perfections,
the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening, the noble truths, the immeasurables, the meditative concentrations, the formless attainments, emptiness, the signless, and the wishless.

One does not perceive the eight liberations, the nine successive meditative attainments, the superknowledges, all the emptinesses, all the concentrations, all the doors of dhāraṇī, the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, from the perspective of the past limit,
nor does one perceive them from the perspective of the future limit.
One does not apprehend [them] in the middle. Thus is the application of non-application. Then, the Venerable Śāriputra said this to the Blessed One:
"Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is profound."
The Blessed One said:
"Śāriputra, the perfection of wisdom is profound because the suchness of form is profound;
so too are feeling, perception, and mental formations."

Śāriputra, because the suchness of consciousness is profound, the perfection of wisdom is profound. In the same way, the elements, the sense bases, dependent origination, the perfections, the factors of enlightenment, the noble truths, the immeasurables, the dhyānas, the formless attainments, the eight liberations, the nine successive meditative attainments,

emptiness, the signless, the wishless, the superknowledges, all the emptinesses, all the samādhis, all the doors of dhāraṇī, the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, and the analytical knowledges are profound.
"Śāriputra, because the suchness of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is profound, the perfection of wisdom is profound.
Thus ends the application regarding profundity.
Śāriputra said:
“Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom.
The Blessed One said:
“Śāriputra, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom because form is difficult to fathom.”

Feeling, perception, and mental formations— Śāriputra, because consciousness is difficult to fathom, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom. Likewise, the elements, the sense bases, dependent origination, the factors of dependent origination, the perfections, all the emptinesses, all the meditative concentrations, and all the doors of dhāraṇī are difficult to fathom.

Śāriputra, because the factors conducive to enlightenment, the noble truths, the immeasurables, the dhyānas, the formless attainments, the eight liberations, the nine successive meditative attainments, emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, the superknowledges, the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are difficult to fathom, the perfection of wisdom is difficult to fathom. Thus is the application of its difficulty to fathom.
Śāriputra said:
"O Bhagavat, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable.
The Bhagavat said:
Śāriputra, because form is immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable;
Śāriputra, because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are immeasurable, the perfection of wisdom is immeasurable. Thus it is.

“Śāriputra, because the elements (*dhātu*), the sense-bases (*āyatana*), the factors of dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpādāṅga*), the perfections (*pāramitā*), all the emptinesses (*śūnyatā*), all the gateways of concentration and mnemonic formulas (*samādhidhāraṇīmukha*), the factors conducive to awakening (*bodhipakṣyadharma*), the noble truths (*āryasatya*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), the meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*), the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*), the eight liberations (*vimokṣa*), the nine successive dwellings and attainments (*navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, the superknowledges (*abhijñā*), the ten powers (*balā*), the fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), and the unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*) are immeasurable, Śāriputra, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) is immeasurable. Thus was the application regarding the immeasurable.
Then Śāriputra said:
"How, Blessed One, does a bodhisattva mahāsattva course in the perfection of wisdom?
The Blessed One said:
"If, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, while coursing in the perfection of wisdom, does not course with the thought that 'form is profound,' then he courses in the perfection of wisdom."
If one does not course in the thought that "feeling, perception, mental formations,
and consciousness are profound," one courses in the perfection of wisdom. Likewise, [one courses in the perfection of wisdom] if one does not course in the elements,

the sense bases, dependent origination, the perfections, the factors of enlightenment, the noble truths, the immeasurables, the meditative absorptions, the formless attainments, the eight liberations, the nine successive meditative dwellings, emptiness, the signless, the wishless, the superknowledges, all samādhis, all doors of dhāraṇī, the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the unique qualities of a Buddha.
If one does not course [with the thought] that "they are profound," one courses in the perfection of wisdom. Why is that?
Because, Śāriputra, that which is the profundity of even all the Buddha-qualities up to those very Buddha-qualities—those are not the Buddha-qualities.
Thus, the "mild" [stage] is another designation for the application of profundity.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of wisdom, he does not practice with the thought that "form is difficult to fathom"; thus he practices the perfection of wisdom. He does not practice with the thought that "feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are difficult to fathom"; thus he practices the perfection of wisdom. In this way...

The elements, the sense bases, dependent origination, the perfections, all the emptinesses, all the samādhis, all the doors of dhāraṇī, the factors conducive to awakening, the noble truths, the immeasurables, the meditative absorptions, the formless attainments, emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, the superknowledges, the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the unique qualities of a Buddha are difficult to fathom; thus, one does not course [in them], yet one courses in the perfection of wisdom. Why is that?
Because, Śāriputra, that which is the difficulty of fathoming the qualities of a Buddha up to the very qualities of a Buddha—those are not the qualities of a Buddha.

Thus, Śāriputra, furthermore, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom does not practice with the thought that "form is immeasurable," he practices the perfection of wisdom; for this is another synonym for the middle way, which is difficult to fathom.

If one does not course in the notion that feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are immeasurable, one courses in the perfection of wisdom. Likewise, if one does not course in the notions that the elements,

the sense bases, dependent origination, the perfections, the factors of enlightenment, the noble truths, the immeasurables, the meditative concentrations, the formless attainments, the eight liberations, the nine successive meditative dwellings, emptiness, the signless, the wishless, the superknowledges, all the emptinesses, all the samādhis, all the doors of dhāraṇī, the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the unique buddha-qualities are immeasurable, one courses in the perfection of wisdom.
One who does not course in the thought that "they are immeasurable" courses in the perfection of wisdom. Why is that?
Because, Śāriputra, as far as the immeasurability of the Buddha-qualities extends, those Buddha-qualities do not exist [as discrete entities].
Thus, the supreme application of the immeasurable is another synonym for this.
Śāriputra said: "Blessed One, since this perfection of wisdom is so profound, difficult to fathom, and immeasurable,
it should not be spoken in the presence of bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have newly set out in the vehicle, lest— "
Upon hearing this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will be terrified, greatly alarmed, and fall into a state of panic.

This [teaching] should be spoken in the presence of an irreversible (*avinivartanīya*) bodhisattva mahāsattva; having heard this *prajñāpāramitā*, he will not be terrified, will not be greatly alarmed, will not fall into a state of panic, will not hesitate, and will not be perplexed.
And having heard it further, one will be liberated.
Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, said this to the venerable Śāriputra:
"Venerable Śāriputra, if this profound perfection of wisdom were to be spoken in the presence of a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has newly set out in the vehicle, what fault would there be?"

Śāriputra said: "Kauśika, if this Perfection of Wisdom were spoken in the presence of a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has newly set out in the vehicle, and he were to be terrified, greatly alarmed, fall into terror, reject it, or repudiate it, and were not to have faith in it."

It is possible, Kauśika, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva who has newly set out in the vehicle, having heard this profound perfection of wisdom, might reject it and accumulate karma leading to the lower realms;

he would then awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment only with great difficulty and after a long time. Thus ends the application regarding the difficulty and the long duration of awakening.

Śakra said: "Furthermore, Reverend Śāriputra, are there any unpredestined bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who, having heard this perfection of wisdom, will not be afraid, will not be terrified, and will not fall into terror?
Śāriputra replied:

“Kauśika, those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, having heard this perfection of wisdom, will not be afraid, will not be terrified, and will not fall into terror, will receive their prophecy of unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment before long.
They will pass by one, two, or three Tathāgatas, and thereafter they will receive their prophecy.”
[This is] for the sake of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable Śāriputra: "It is so, Śāriputra, it is so."

“Śāriputra, those bodhisattva mahāsattvas will have set out for a long time; Śāriputra, those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who, having heard this profound perfection of wisdom, do not tremble, are not terrified, and do not fall into fear, will have practiced the six perfections for a long time and will have attended upon many Buddhas.”
And having heard it further, they will take it up, bear it in mind, recite it, master it, and abide in the perfection of wisdom exactly as it has been taught.
Then, the venerable Śāriputra said this to the Blessed One:
"It occurs to me, Blessed One; it occurs to me, Sugata.
The Blessed One said: "Let it occur to you."
Śāriputra said: "Blessed One, it is just as if a son of good family or a daughter of good family who has set out in the Great Vehicle were to practice the perfection of wisdom while in a dream,
or were to practice the perfection of meditation, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of patience, the perfection of ethical discipline, and the perfection of generosity."

"O Blessed One, it should be known that as long as he remains seated at the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*), this son of good family or daughter of good family is drawing near to unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening (*anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi*). How much more so, O Blessed One, for one who, having awakened, cultivates the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*)?"

“Blessed One, it should be known that when one cultivates the perfection of meditation, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of patience, the perfection of ethical discipline, and the perfection of generosity, this son of good family or daughter of good family is drawing near to unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Thus is the application for obtaining the prophecy;
Blessed One, those sons of good family and daughters of good family will have fully ripened roots of virtue.”

Those who shall obtain this profound *prajñāpāramitā* for the sake of hearing it, and having heard it, shall practice accordingly—those sons of good family and daughters of good family, O Blessed One, will have long since set out in the vehicle; they will have planted roots of merit, served many Buddhas, and been sustained by spiritual friends.
Those sons of good family and daughters of good family, O Blessed One, who, having heard this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, shall take it up, bear it in mind, and recite it...

They will master it and attend to it with wise attention. Blessed One, those sons of good family and daughters of good family will be near to the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, or they have already been predicted; or else those sons of good family and daughters of good family are irreversible from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.
Those for whom this perfection of wisdom will arise spontaneously, and having arisen, they will take it up, bear it in mind, recite it, master it, and attend to it with proper mental reflection—
this is the application of those who are irreversible.
It is just as if, Blessed One, a person were to emerge from a wilderness forest extending for a hundred leagues.

Having emerged from a wilderness of two hundred yojanas, three hundred yojanas, four hundred yojanas, or five hundred yojanas, and having emerged, he would see the prior signs of a village, a city, or a market town— namely, cowherds, shepherds,
boundaries, groves, forests, parks, the signs of parks, or villages.

Or, having seen the preliminary signs of villages, cities, market towns, royal capitals, or kingdoms, he thinks: "Since these preliminary signs of a village, city, market town, royal capital, or kingdom are now visible, those places must be near. He would thereby find reassurance.
Furthermore, he will no longer have fear of thieves, fear of outcasts, fear of fierce wild animals,

fear of hunger, or fear of thirst. In the same way, Blessed One, for that bodhisattva mahāsattva in whom this profound perfection of wisdom arises spontaneously, and having arisen, he takes it up and retains it—

"Blessed One, it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva will be near to receiving the prophecy of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; he will not be long before he awakens to it. Furthermore, that bodhisattva mahāsattva should not be afraid."
"Neither from the level of a śrāvaka nor from the level of a pratyekabuddha. Why is that?
Because these are the preceding signs, namely, that a bodhisattva mahāsattva obtains this profound perfection of wisdom for the purpose of seeing, worshipping, attending upon, and hearing it.
When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable Śāriputra:
"So it is, Śāriputra; so it is. Let the application for departure occur to you further, Śāriputra, through the power of the Buddha.
Śāriputra said:
It is just as if, Blessed One, a man should desire to see the great ocean;
he would go toward the great ocean for the purpose of seeing it. As he goes toward the great ocean, so he would see a tree or the sign of a tree, or a mountain or the sign of a mountain.
By this he should know: "The great ocean is still far from here; it is not near."
This is the great ocean. For what reason?
Because in the vicinity of the great ocean, no tree or sign of a tree, nor any mountain or sign of a mountain, is seen. It is just as if, Blessed One, a man should desire to see the great ocean.
Just as he proceeds toward the great ocean to behold it, so too he does not see a tree or the sign of a tree, nor a mountain or the sign of a mountain.
It occurs to him: "The great ocean is not far from here; the great ocean is near. Why is that?
Because in the vicinity of the great ocean, no tree or the sign of a tree, nor any mountain or the sign of a mountain, is seen.

Furthermore, although that person does not see the great ocean with his eyes, he nevertheless reaches a certainty: "I am near the great ocean; the great ocean is close to me; the great ocean is not far from here; the great ocean is no further away than this. In the same way, Blessed One, that bodhisattva mahāsattva should understand thus:

While hearing, taking up, retaining, reciting, mastering, and properly attending to this perfection of wisdom, one should reflect thus: "Even though I have not been personally prophesied by that Blessed One regarding unsurpassed,
perfect, and complete enlightenment— specifying such-and-such eons, such-and-so many hundreds of eons, such-and-so many thousands of eons..."

"After this many hundreds of thousands of kalpas, indeed after this many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas, you will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Furthermore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should understand it in this way:
"I have drawn near to the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. For what reason?
Because I have obtained this profound perfection of wisdom for the purpose of seeing, worshipping, attending upon, and hearing it;
and having heard it, I take it up, bear it in mind, recite it, master it, and attend to it with wise reflection.
Thus is the unsurpassed application.
For example, Blessed One, when spring has arrived and the stalks have shed their withered leaves and sprouts have begun to emerge,
it should be known by the people of Jambudvīpa that before long there will be leaves, flowers, and fruits.
They will come forth. For what reason?
These very portents are seen upon the stalks; before long, leaves, flowers, and fruits will appear, and the people of Jambudvīpa will become joyful upon seeing those portents on the stalks.

In the same way, Blessed One, that bodhisattva mahāsattva who obtains this profound perfection of wisdom for the purpose of seeing, saluting, attending upon, and hearing it—and having heard it, takes it up, bears it in mind, recites it, masters it, and attends to it with wise reflection—should be known, Blessed One, as a bodhisattva mahāsattva whose roots of virtue are fully ripened.
That son of good family or daughter of good family, Blessed One, should be known as one who has attended upon many Buddhas. This should be understood.
"O Blessed One, it is because of my former roots of merit that I have been brought by that bodhisattva mahāsattva to this unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment,
I who now obtain this profound perfection of wisdom for the purpose of seeing, honoring, attending upon, and hearing it."
And when one practices according to the Prajñāpāramitā as it has been taught, there, O sons of gods, those who have seen previous Buddhas become joyful;

filled with joy and gladness of mind, they think: "These very same preliminary signs occurred for previous Bodhisattvas, Mahāsattvas, prior to their prophecy; before long, this Bodhisattva, Mahāsattva..."
He will receive the prophecy of his unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
This is the practice for approaching full awakening;
just as, Blessed One, when a pregnant woman draws near to her time of delivery, her body becomes increasingly constrained and she experiences intense physical pain and exhaustion.
She does not have the habit of walking about, she has little mindfulness, and she eats little food.
She has little sloth and torpor; experiencing those present feelings, she speaks little and does not have a habit of socializing.

"Because of that former improper mental attention (*ayoniśo-manasikāra*) which was practiced, cultivated, and pursued, I experience such a feeling as this. It should be understood that just as one perceives the signs of another woman, one knows:
"In no long time this woman will give birth. In the same way, Blessed One, it is for the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas.
To those who have planted roots of merit, who have attended upon many Buddhas, who have practiced well-conducted conduct, who are sustained by spiritual friends,
and whose roots of merit are fully ripened— this profound perfection of wisdom will become accessible; and once it has become accessible,
they will take it up, bear it in mind, recite it, master it, and attend to it with wise reflection.

"It should be known that before long these bodhisattva mahāsattvas will receive the prophecy of their unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening. The Blessed One said, "Excellent, excellent, Śāriputra! This inspired eloquence of yours, Śāriputra, has also arisen through the power of the Buddha. Thus concludes the application for swift awakening.
Then the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:
"It is marvelous, Blessed One, how these bodhisattva mahāsattvas have been so favored and so well-sustained by the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened Buddha."
The Blessed One said: "For it is thus, Subhūti, that bodhisattvas mahāsattvas have set out for the welfare of many people, for the happiness of many people,
out of compassion for the world, for the sake, welfare, and happiness of the great multitude of beings— both gods and humans— for the sake of unsurpassed [enlightenment]."

Establishing themselves in *samyaksaṃbodhi* while practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, they will benefit many hundreds of beings, many thousands of beings, many hundreds of thousands of beings, and many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of beings; through the four means of attraction— generosity, pleasant speech, purposeful action, and consistency of purpose— they will encourage them toward the ten paths of wholesome action.

They encourage others to take up the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, and they themselves become established in these dharmas. They themselves practice the perfection of generosity and establish others in the perfection of generosity; they themselves practice the perfection of ethical discipline and [establish others] in the perfection of ethical discipline.

They establish others [in them]. They themselves practice the perfection of patience and establish others in the perfection of patience; they themselves practice the perfection of vigor and establish others in the perfection of vigor;
they themselves practice the perfection of meditation and establish others in the perfection of meditation.
They themselves practice the perfection of wisdom and establish others in the perfection of wisdom.

Relying upon that perfection of wisdom and through skill in means, they establish sentient beings in the fruit of stream-entry, yet they do not personally realize it for themselves. Likewise, [they establish them] in the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and arhatship.
They establish others in individual enlightenment, yet they do not personally realize individual enlightenment for themselves.
They themselves advance to the stage of non-retrogression and establish others on the stage of non-retrogression.
They themselves purify a buddha-field, and...

They encourage other bodhisattvas toward the purification of the buddha-field. They themselves bring sentient beings to maturity and encourage others toward the maturation of sentient beings. They themselves generate the superknowledges and encourage others to attain the superknowledges. They themselves purify the gateway of the dhāraṇīs and [encourage] others as well toward the purification of the gateway of the dhāraṇīs.

They encourage others. They themselves attain the perfection of eloquence and also encourage others to attain the perfection of eloquence. They themselves embrace the perfection of form and also encourage others to attain the perfection of form. They themselves embrace the perfection of the marks and also [encourage others] (PSP_4:21).

They encourage others to attain the perfection of the marks [of a Great Man]. They themselves embrace the perfection of the state of a youth (kumārabhūta), and they also encourage others to embrace the perfection of the state of a youth. They themselves accomplish the factors conducive to awakening (bodhipakṣyadharma), and they also encourage others toward the complete accomplishment of the factors conducive to awakening. They themselves [cultivate] the truths, the liberations, the nine successive meditative attainments (anupūrvavihārasamāpatti), emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, and the gateways of mnemonic formulas (dhāraṇīmukha).

They generate [these qualities] themselves and also encourage others to undertake them. They themselves generate the four grounds of self-confidence (*vaiśāradya*) and also encourage others to undertake the four grounds of self-confidence. They themselves generate the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) and also encourage others to attain the four analytical knowledges. They themselves generate great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*) and great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*)...

They cultivate great sympathetic joy and great equanimity, and they also encourage others to cultivate the four immeasurables. They themselves accomplish the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and they also encourage others toward those eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. They themselves attain the knowledge of all aspects, and they [encourage] others toward the knowledge of all aspects.

They encourage others. They themselves abandon all afflictions along with their underlying tendencies and connections, and they also encourage others to abandon all afflictions along with their underlying tendencies and connections. They themselves realize unexcelled perfect enlightenment, and they encourage others to realize unexcelled perfect enlightenment. They themselves turn the wheel of Dharma, and they encourage others to turn the wheel of Dharma.
They encourage [others] to engage in it.
Such is the application for the sake of others.
When this had been said, the Venerable Subhūti addressed the Blessed One as follows:

“It is marvelous, Blessed One! It is marvelous, Sugata! To what extent those bodhisattva mahāsattvas are endowed with many virtues who, for the sake of all sentient beings, course in the perfection of wisdom and realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening!
How, Blessed One, does the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom by bodhisattva mahāsattvas reach fulfillment?”
The Blessed One said: "Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, coursing in the perfection of wisdom, does not perceive the increase of form,
nor of feeling, nor of perception, nor of mental formations;
When he does not perceive an increase in consciousness,
then the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s cultivation of the perfection of wisdom reaches fulfillment.
The Blessed One said:

Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, does not [perceive] the elements, the sense bases, dependent origination and its factors, the perfections, the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening, the noble truths, the immeasurables, the meditative absorptions, the formless attainments, the eight liberations, the nine successive meditative dwellings, or the six [perfections]— emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness— [he courses in the perfection of wisdom].

He does not perceive an increase in the superknowledges (*abhijñā*), all the emptinesses (*śūnyatā*), all the meditative concentrations (*samādhi*), all the gateways of the dhāraṇīs (*dhāraṇīmukha*), the ten powers (*bala*), the four grounds of self-confidence (*vaiśāradya*), the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), or the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*).
When he does not perceive an increase in omniscience,
then the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s cultivation of the perfection of wisdom reaches fulfillment.
The Blessed One said:

And when, Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, coursing in the perfection of wisdom, does not perceive the diminution of form, nor the diminution of feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness;

Then the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom of the bodhisattva mahāsattva reaches fulfillment. Likewise, when he does not perceive any diminution of omniscience regarding the elements, the sense bases, dependent origination, the perfections, the factors of enlightenment, the noble truths, the immeasurables, the meditative concentrations, the formless attainments, the eight liberations, the nine successive meditative dwellings, emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, the superknowledges, all samādhis, all doors of dhāraṇī, the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the unique qualities of a buddha— [then his cultivation of the perfection of wisdom reaches fulfillment].
Then the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom of the bodhisattva mahāsattva reaches fulfillment. This is the application regarding neither increase nor decrease.
Furthermore, Subhūti, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva, practicing in the perfection of wisdom, does not perceive "dharma" and does not perceive "non-dharma," [then his cultivation reaches fulfillment].
He does not perceive it as past, he does not perceive it as future, and he does not perceive it as present.
He does not perceive it as wholesome, unwholesome, determinate, or indeterminate;
he does not perceive it as conditioned,
nor does he perceive it as unconditioned.
He does not perceive the desire realm, he does not perceive the form realm,
and he does not perceive the formless realm.
He does not perceive the perfection of generosity, he does not perceive the perfection of ethical discipline,
and he does not perceive the perfection of patience.
He does not perceive the perfection of vigor; he does not perceive the perfection of meditation;
he does not perceive the perfection of wisdom; and so on, up to: he does not perceive omniscience.
Then the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s cultivation of the perfection of wisdom reaches fulfillment. Why is that?

Because, Subhūti, it is by taking recourse to the dharma-characteristic of phenomena, by taking recourse to their irreversibility, by taking recourse to their emptiness, by taking recourse to their vanity, by taking recourse to their lack of core, and by taking recourse to their insubstantiality—this is the practice of the non-apprehension of phenomena and so forth.
Subhūti said:
"The inconceivable, O Blessed One, is being taught.
The Blessed One said:
Subhūti, because form is inconceivable, the inconceivable is taught;

because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are inconceivable, Subhūti, the inconceivable is taught. Because the perfection of generosity is inconceivable, the inconceivable is taught.

In this way, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom are taught as inconceivable because they are inconceivable.

Likewise, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the noble truths, the immeasurables, the meditative absorptions, the formless attainments, the eight liberations, the nine successive attainments, emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, the superknowledges, all the emptinesses, all the samādhis, all the doors of dhāraṇī, the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the unique qualities of a buddha [are taught as inconceivable].
Subhūti, because omniscience is inconceivable, it is taught as inconceivable. Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva,
while practicing the perfection of wisdom, does not perceive that form is inconceivable,
nor feeling, perception, or mental formations;

One who does not perceive that consciousness is inconceivable will fulfill the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). In this same way, [one will fulfill] the elements (*dhātu*), the sense bases (*āyatana*), dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*), the factors of dependent origination, the perfections, the emptinesses, all meditative concentrations (*samādhi*), all doors of retention (*dhāraṇīmukha*),

the factors conducive to enlightenment (*bodhipakṣyadharma*), the noble truths, the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), the dhyānas, the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*), the eight liberations (*vimokṣa*), the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), the [three] gateways of liberation— emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness— the superknowledges (*abhijñā*), the ten powers (*bala*), the fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), and the unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*).
Thinking, "The omniscience is inconceivable," he does not perceive it, yet he will fulfill the perfection of wisdom.
This is the application for the cessation of the perception of inconceivable forms.
Subhūti said:
"Lord, who will have faith in this profound perfection of wisdom?
The Blessed One replied:
"Subhūti, it is that bodhisattva mahāsattva who has already practiced in the past."
He has planted roots of merit under the Tathāgatas regarding the six perfections;
he has attended upon many Buddhas and is sustained by spiritual friends;
he gains resolute conviction in this perfection of wisdom.
Subhūti said: "To what extent, Blessed One, does a bodhisattva mahāsattva become one who has previously practiced, and one who has planted roots of merit under the Tathāgatas in the six perfections?"
He has attended upon many Buddhas and is sustained by spiritual friends.
The Blessed One said:
"In this regard, Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of wisdom does not conceptualize form, nor does he discriminate it."
One does not conceptualize or discriminate the sign of form; one does not conceptualize or discriminate the intrinsic nature of form;
[and likewise for] feeling, perception, and mental formations.
One does not conceptualize or discriminate consciousness;

one does not conceptualize or discriminate the signs of consciousness; one does not conceptualize or discriminate the intrinsic nature of consciousness. In the same way, [one does not conceptualize or discriminate] the elements, the sense bases, and dependent origination.

The factors of dependent origination, the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm; the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom; and internal emptiness, external emptiness, and internal-external emptiness.

As long as he does not conceptualize or discriminate the emptiness of non-existence and essential nature, nor the applications of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of miraculous power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, the path, the noble truths, the immeasurables, the meditative concentrations, the formless attainments, the eight liberations, the nine successive meditative dwellings, the attainments of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, the superknowledges, all samādhis, all doors of dhāraṇī, the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, the unique qualities of a Buddha, or omniscience;
One does not conceptualize or discriminate the sign of omniscience, nor does one conceptualize or discriminate the intrinsic nature of omniscience. Why is that?
Because, Subhūti, form is inconceivable.

Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are inconceivable. Likewise, the elements, the sense bases, dependent origination, the perfections, the factors conducive to awakening, the noble truths, the immeasurables, the meditative concentrations, the formless attainments, the eight liberations, the nine successive meditative dwellings, emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, the superknowledges, all the emptinesses, all the samādhis, all the doors of dhāraṇī, the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the unique qualities of a Buddha are inconceivable.

Omniscience is inconceivable. In this way, Subhūti, a bodhisattva mahāsattva has indeed previously practiced the six perfections; he has planted roots of merit under the Tathāgatas, has attended upon many Buddhas, and has been sustained by spiritual friends.
Subhūti said:
"O Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is profound.
The Blessed One said:
Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is profound because form is profound;
Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is profound because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are profound. Thus it is.

Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is profound because of the profundity of the elements (*dhātu*), the sense-bases (*āyatana*), dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*), the perfections (*pāramitā*), the factors conducive to awakening (*bodhipakṣyadharma*), the noble truths (*āryasatya*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), the meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*), the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*), the eight liberations (*vimokṣa*), the nine successive dwellings in attainment (*navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, the superknowledges (*abhijñā*), all forms of emptiness, all samādhis, all doors of dhāraṇī, the ten powers (*daśabala*), the fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), and the unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*).
Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is profound because of the profundity of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*). This is the application of non-conceptuality (*avikalpaprayoga*).
Subhūti said:

"O Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is a heap of jewels; it is the giver of jewels, [bestowing] the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, arhatship, the state of a pratyekabuddha, and unsurpassed [perfect enlightenment]."
“O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is the giver of perfect enlightenment and the turner of the wheel of Dharma. Thus concludes the application for the gift of the jewel of the fruit.
Subhūti said:
“O Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is the pure mass of all phenomena.”
The Blessed One said:
"Based on the purity of form, [there is] the purity of feeling, perception, and mental formations."

Based on the purity of consciousness. Likewise, based on the purity of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), there are the elements (*dhātu*), the sense-bases (*āyatana*), dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*), the perfections (*pāramitā*), the factors conducive to awakening (*bodhipakṣyadharma*), the noble truths (*āryasatya*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), the meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*), the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*), the eight liberations (*vimokṣa*), the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), emptiness (*śūnyatā*), signlessness (*animitta*), wishlessness (*apraṇihita*), the superknowledges (*abhijñā*), the ten powers (*daśabala*), the fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), and the unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*). This is the application of purification.
Subhūti said:
"It is wonderful, Blessed One, that while this profound perfection of wisdom is being taught, so many obstacles should arise.
The Blessed One said:
"So it is, Subhūti; so it is.
This profound perfection of wisdom, Subhūti, is subject to many obstacles.
Therefore, that son of good family or daughter of good family who has written out this perfection of wisdom should write it out very quickly."
By one who points it out, upholds it, recites it, studies it, attends to it with wise reflection, and cultivates it,
it should be cultivated very swiftly. Indeed, while this profound perfection of wisdom is being written down, pointed out, upheld, recited, studied, and attended to with wise reflection—
"Or there might be an obstacle while it is being cultivated. For what reason?

Subhūti, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to write this Perfection of Wisdom in one month, it should indeed be written by them. Or if [they write it] in two, three, four, five, six, or seven months..."

Whether one should write it in eight months or even in a year, it must indeed be written; likewise, it should be taught, upheld, recited, studied, and properly attended to with right attention. If one should cultivate it for a month, it should be cultivated by that person;
or if one should cultivate it for a year, it should be cultivated by that person. For what reason?
"Subhūti, many obstacles arise for a great jewel.
Subhūti said:
"It is marvelous, Blessed One, that Māra the Evil One exerts himself to create obstacles for this profound perfection of wisdom."
That is to say: for the sake of not writing it down, not directing [the mind] toward it, not retaining it, not reciting it, not attending to it properly, and not cultivating it.
The Blessed One said:
"Moreover, Subhūti, even if Māra, the Evil One, should exert himself to create an obstacle to this profound perfection of wisdom..."

For the purpose of writing— that is, from the act of copying up to the cultivation— of this profound perfection of wisdom by a bodhisattva mahāsattva who is writing, teaching, retaining, reciting, studying, correctly attending to, and cultivating it, no one is able to create an obstacle.
Thus has the application of resolute belief been explained. Now, the Venerable Śāriputra said this to the Blessed One:
"By whose power, Blessed One, is Māra the Evil One unable to create obstacles for the Bodhisattvas?"
"For the great beings who write down, point out, preserve, recite, study, properly attend to, and cultivate this profound perfection of wisdom?
The Blessed One said:

By the power of the Buddha, Śāriputra, Māra the Evil One is unable to create obstacles for those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who write down, teach, retain, recite, study, correctly attend to, and cultivate this profound perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Śāriputra, those who [are] all around in the ten directions...
In all directions, the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, reside, remain, and maintain themselves;

it is through the power of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, that they too will attend to and sustain those bodhisattva mahāsattvas. And for those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who are sustained by those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, Māra, the Evil One, is unable to create any obstacle.
For those who write, preserve, recite, explain, study, correctly attend to, and cultivate this perfection of wisdom. Why is that?
Śāriputra, it is because Māra, the Evil One, is unable to create obstacles for those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who are sustained by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones. Why is that?

Śāriputra, as for their Dharma— even those immeasurable and incalculable Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Buddhas who, throughout the immeasurable and incalculable world-systems in all ten directions,
currently abide, remain, and maintain themselves—
those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, [protect] one who writes, upholds, recites, or teaches this perfection of wisdom.
They attend to those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who engage in private recitation, who attend to the teachings with proper mental attention, and who cultivate them.
Thus, Śāriputra, that son of good family or daughter of good family should understand this as the quality of obstructing the power of Māra regarding this profound perfection of wisdom.

Whether writing, or retaining, or reciting, or teaching, or studying, or attending to it with wise reflection, or cultivating it, it is through the power of the Buddhas that I write this profound perfection of wisdom, retain it, recite it, teach it, study it, cultivate it, and attend to it with wise reflection.

Śāriputra said: "Blessed One, if any son of good family or daughter of good family shall write down, preserve, recite, explain, study, properly attend to, and cultivate this profound perfection of wisdom,"
"Blessed One, it should be understood that all of this is through the power of the Buddhas,
and all of them will be sustained by the Buddhas."
The Blessed One said:
"So it is, Śāriputra, so it is, just as you say: whichever son of good family or daughter of good family [upholds] this profound perfection of wisdom..."

Śāriputra, it should be known that whoever shall write, preserve, recite, teach, study, attend to with wise reflection, and cultivate [this teaching], all that will be through the power of the Buddhas; they shall all be sustained by the Buddhas.
Thus is the quality of making known the Buddhas' mindful attention.
Śāriputra said:

"O Blessed One, those sons of good family and daughters of good family have been known by you through your wisdom; O Blessed One, those sons of good family and daughters of good family who are in the eastern direction, as far as [the limit], have been seen by those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, with their fleshly eyes."
In the immeasurable and incalculable world-systems in the ten directions, immeasurable and incalculable Tathāgatas, Arhats,
and Samyaksaṃbuddhas currently reside, remain, and maintain their lives;
and those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who shall write down and uphold this profound Prajñāpāramitā—
They will read it, recite it, study it, cultivate it, attend to it with wise reflection, and practice in accordance with suchness.
The Blessed One said: "So it is, Śāriputra; so it is."

Śāriputra, those sons of good family and daughters of good family are known by me through my wisdom; Śāriputra, those sons of good family and daughters of good family are seen by me with my fleshly eye— those immeasurable and incalculable Tathāgatas, Arhats, who are in the immeasurable and incalculable world-systems throughout the ten directions, as far as the eastern direction, by those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.
The perfectly awakened Buddhas remain, stay, and maintain themselves;

and those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who will write down, preserve, recite, teach, study, cultivate, and attend to this profound perfection of wisdom with wise reflection— [for them, the Buddhas provide their protection].
They will practice for the sake of suchness. This is the quality of bringing [the Dharma] directly before the eyes of the Buddhas.
Furthermore, those sons of good family and daughters of good family belonging to the Mahāyāna should be known as having drawn near to unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
This is the quality of bringing them close to perfect enlightenment.
