Moreover, Śāriputra, those sons of good family and daughters of good family who, having written down this profound perfection of wisdom and made it into a book, shall preserve it— those sons of good family and daughters of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle, Śāriputra, will indeed possess great resolute faith in this profound perfection of wisdom here.

Moreover, Śāriputra, those sons of good family and daughters of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who shall honor, revere, respect, and worship this profound perfection of wisdom with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, banners, and flags—they too are known and seen by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones; and the Tathāgatas behold them with their Buddha-eye.
For those sons of good family and daughters of good family, there will be great purpose, great benefit, great fruit, and great maturation.

Those who, having written down this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, shall uphold it, will by that root of merit never be separated from the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones. They shall never be reborn in the lower realms;
being reborn among gods and humans, they shall never be separated from the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and they shall transcend the stage of non-retrogression.
And those sons of good family or daughters of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle shall, by that very root of merit, never be separated from the six perfections;
they shall never be separated from internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-external emptiness, up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence;

and they shall never be separated from the applications of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of miraculous power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, the path, the noble truths, the meditative concentrations, the immeasurables, and the formless attainments.

They shall never be separated from the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; they shall never be separated from the eight liberations and the nine successive meditative attainments;
and they shall never be separated from the superknowledges, the concentrations, and the gateways of the dhāraṇīs.

They shall never be separated from the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four grounds of self-confidence, the four analytical knowledges, and so on up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, nor from omniscience.
Thus are the qualities such as great purposefulness.
Moreover, Śāriputra, after the passing of the Tathāgata, this Prajñāpāramitā will circulate in the southern region.
There, monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen will write down, take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and properly attend to this profound Prajñāpāramitā. By that root of merit, they...
They will not go to a state of woe or downfall; experiencing the prosperity of gods and humans, they will advance by means of the six perfections.

Honoring, respecting, revering, and worshiping the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, they will gradually attain final nirvana through one of the three vehicles—namely, the vehicle of the disciples, the vehicle of the solitary buddhas, or the Great Vehicle.

"Śāriputra, this profound perfection of wisdom will spread from the southern region to Vartanī. There too, monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen will write down, take up, and preserve this profound perfection of wisdom."

They will recite it, master it, and attend to it properly; they will honor, revere, respect, and worship it with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, banners, and flags.
By that root of merit, they shall not go to a state of woe or downfall.
Experiencing the prosperity of gods and humans, they will be preeminent through the six perfections;

honoring, revering, respecting, and worshipping the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, they will gradually go forth by means of the three vehicles— whether by the vehicle of the disciples, the vehicle of the solitary buddhas, or the Great Vehicle.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, this profound perfection of wisdom will circulate in the northern region of Vartanī;
there too, Śāriputra, monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen will write down, take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and properly attend to this profound perfection of wisdom.
By that root of merit, they will not go to a state of woe or ruin;
having experienced the prosperity of gods and humans, they will become exalted through the six perfections,
and they will honor, revere, respect, and worship the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.
They will go forth by means of the three vehicles in due order—whether by the vehicle of the disciples, the vehicle of the solitary buddhas, or the Great Vehicle.
In this regard, Śāriputra, this profound perfection of wisdom will perform the work of a Buddha. Why is that?
Because, Śāriputra, as long as the Dharma and Vinaya have reached their full maturity, there shall be no disappearance of the True Dharma.

Śāriputra, those sons of good family and daughters of good family who will write down, take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and properly attend to this profound perfection of wisdom, and who will practice for the sake of suchness— they have been taken into my care.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, those sons of good family and daughters of good family who shall write down this profound perfection of wisdom, and having written it down, shall honor, revere, respect, and worship it with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, banners, and flags— by that root of merit, those sons of good family and daughters of good family shall not fall into the miserable states of existence.
Having experienced the prosperity of gods and humans, they will become exalted through the six perfections;

having become exalted, they will honor, revere, respect, and worship the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and will gradually go forth by means of the three vehicles—whether by the vehicle of the disciples, the vehicle of the solitary buddhas, or the Great Vehicle. For what reason is that?

For, Śāriputra, those sons of good family and daughters of good family have been seen by the Tathāgata with his Buddha-eye; they have been described by the Tathāgata, they have been praised by the Tathāgata— those who,
throughout the entire expanse of world-systems in the ten directions, [take refuge in] the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who currently reside there.

Those sons of good family and daughters of good family are seen by those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones who currently abide and maintain their lives; they have been beheld with the Buddha-eye and praised, and those sons of good family and daughters of good family have been commended.
Śāriputra said:
"Furthermore, Blessed One, this profound perfection of wisdom will be widespread in the northern direction in the future time, in the final age.
The Blessed One said: "So it is, Śāriputra; so it is."

Śāriputra, in the future time, in the final age, this profound perfection of wisdom will become widespread in the northern direction. In that regard, Śāriputra, in the future time, in the final age, those sons of good family and daughters of good family who hear this profound perfection of wisdom and, having heard it, write it down—
They will take it up, bear it in mind, recite it, master it, attend to it with wise reflection, and practice in accordance with suchness.

Those sons of good family and daughters of good family who hear this profound perfection of wisdom and, having heard it, [act accordingly] have long since set out in the vehicle; they have attended upon many Buddhas and have planted roots of merit under those Tathāgatas.
And they will write it down, take it up, bear it in mind, recite it, master it, attend to it with wise reflection, and practice in accordance with suchness.
Śāriputra said:
"Blessed One, how many sons of good family or daughters of good family will there be who,
in the future time, in the final age, in the northern direction, having heard this profound perfection of wisdom,
will write it down, take it up, bear it in mind, recite it, master it, and attend to it with wise reflection?"
And they will practice for the sake of suchness.
The Blessed One said:
"Moreover, Śāriputra, although in the future time, in the final period, there will be many bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas in the northern direction,"

Moreover, Śāriputra, there will be few sons of good family and daughters of good family who, having heard this profound perfection of wisdom, will write it down, take it up, bear it in mind, recite it, master it, attend to it properly, and practice in accordance with suchness.
Such is the merit of defining the location.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, those sons of good family and daughters of good family who, having heard this profound perfection of wisdom being taught, shall not be afraid, nor shall they be terrified.
They will not fall into terror. Why is that?
Because those sons of good family and daughters of good family have followed after the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, having questioned them and having interrogated them. Why is that?

Because those sons of good family and daughters of good family will have fulfilled the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā). Likewise, they will have fulfilled the perfection of meditation (dhyānapāramitā), the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā), the perfection of patience (kṣāntipāramitā), and the perfection of ethical discipline (śīlapāramitā).
Those sons of good family and daughters of good family will be perfected in the perfection of generosity;
those sons of good family and daughters of good family will be perfected in internal emptiness;
and those sons of good family and daughters of good family will be perfected in external emptiness.
Those sons of good family and daughters of good family will be perfected in internal and external emptiness,
and those sons of good family and daughters of good family will be perfected in everything up to the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence.
Likewise, they will be perfected in the applications of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold path.
And those sons of good family and daughters of good family will become perfected in the immeasurable meditative concentrations and formless attainments;
and those sons of good family and daughters of good family will become perfected in the noble truths.
Those sons of good family and daughters of good family will be perfected in the eight liberations and the nine successive meditative attainments;

those sons of good family and daughters of good family will be perfected in emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, and the superknowledges; and those sons of good family and daughters of good family will be perfected in the gateways of meditative concentration and mnemonic formulas.

Those sons of good family and daughters of good family will be perfected in the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the unique qualities of a Buddha. Furthermore, Śāriputra, those sons of good family and daughters of good family, supported by their roots of merit,
will act for the benefit of many people.
This is with reference to this unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Thus is the quality of fulfilling all untainted dharmas.
Why is that?
For in that place, I have spoken only discourse connected with omniscience for those sons of good family and daughters of good family;

and those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who appeared in the past— by those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, too, only discourse connected with omniscience was spoken for those sons of good family and daughters of good family, even as they passed through their various births.
They will act in such a manner,
namely with reference to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment,
that they will speak to others in exactly that same way.
That is to say, starting from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
(PSP_4:32) Thus is the quality of being a person of discourse.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, those sons of good family and daughters of good family who are bodhisattvas will indeed be gathered together.

They cannot be diverted from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by Māra, or by the deities belonging to Māra’s host, much less by others who are evil-minded and of wicked conduct— those who shall obtain this profound perfection of wisdom.
This is the quality of being indivisible.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, those bodhisattvas, sons of good family, and daughters of good family, having heard this perfection of wisdom, will attain sublime joy, serene confidence, and gladness. And they will establish many people in roots of goodness,
namely, by means of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment itself.
Such is the quality of the arising of uncommon roots of virtue;
and thus those sons of good family and daughters of good family have spoken these words in my presence:
"O Blessed One, we [shall lead] many hundreds of living beings, many thousands of living beings, many hundreds of thousands of living beings."

We shall establish many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of living beings in roots of virtue, namely, with reference to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. We shall establish them in awakening; we shall demonstrate it to them, incite them toward it, inspire them, gladden them, and we shall grant them the prophecy of their non-retrogression. Why is that?
I have rejoiced in the words spoken by those sons of good family and daughters of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle, having observed their minds with my own mind.
In the presence of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones of the past as well, those sons of good family and daughters of good family spoke thus:
"We [shall lead] many hundreds of beings, many thousands of beings, many hundreds of thousands of beings, and many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of beings."

"Practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, we shall establish them in awakening, show it to them, encourage them, inspire them, gladden them, and we shall prophesy their non-retrogression. Why is that?

Because the speech uttered by those sons of good family and daughters of good family—those bodhisattvas—was rejoiced in by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones of the past, both in word and in thought."

Having observed their minds, Śāriputra, I indeed rejoiced in those sons of good family and daughters of good family, saying: "These bodhisattva mahāsattvas, practicing for the sake of awakening, [will lead] many hundreds of beings, many thousands of beings, and many hundreds of thousands of beings."
They will establish many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of living beings in unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
they will demonstrate it to them, incite them toward it, inspire them, gladden them, and grant them the prophecy of non-retrogression.
This is the quality of fulfilling one's promise according to its true meaning.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, those sons of good family and daughters of good family will possess noble aspirations;
they will give noble gifts regarding forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena.
Having given noble gifts, they will cultivate noble roots of merit. Having cultivated noble roots of merit, they will take possession of a noble maturation.
Having taken hold of that sublime maturation, they will take hold of maturation after maturation for the sake of those very same beings.
This is their quality of taking hold of the sublime fruit:
they relinquish all things for the sake of all those very beings.
Whether they be internal or external, by that root of merit he will take hold of other Buddha-fields where the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are present and teaching the Dharma.
Having heard this very Perfection of Wisdom in those [fields], there too in that Buddha-field, many hundreds of beings— many...

They will demonstrate, encourage, inspire, and gladden many thousands of living beings, many hundreds of thousands of living beings, and many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of living beings for the sake of unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. Śāriputra said:

It is marvelous, Blessed One, that there is no dharma whatsoever which has not been known by the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha; there is no suchness of dharmas whatsoever which has not been known; and there is no conduct of sentient beings whatsoever which has not been known.
For indeed, even the Tathāgatas of the past—their Bodhisattvas, Buddha-fields, and Śrāvakas—are unknown; even the Tathāgatas of the future—their Bodhisattvas, Buddha-fields, and Śrāvakas—are unknown;
and even the Tathāgatas of the present—their Bodhisattvas, Buddha-fields, and Śrāvakas—are unknown.

Furthermore, those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who reside, remain, and maintain themselves in the world-systems of the ten directions, and who teach the Dharma— even for those Tathāgatas,
Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, the Bodhisattvas, Buddha-fields, and Śrāvakas are unknown [to them].
This is the quality of practicing for the benefit of sentient beings.

Blessed One, those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who shall apply themselves with diligence for the sake of these six perfections will also seek and search for these six perfections. Furthermore, for those sons of good family, [the Tathāgata will reveal them].
"And among these daughters of good family who seek and search for these six perfections, will some obtain these six perfections and others not obtain them?
The Blessed One said:
"Śāriputra, for the most part, all these six perfections will arise for those sons of good family and daughters of good family. Why is that?
Because, Śāriputra, those sons of good family and daughters of good family have applied themselves with diligence to these six perfections.
Śāriputra said:
"But, Blessed One, will these very deep sūtras connected with the six perfections appear to those sons of good family and daughters of good family?
The Blessed One said:
"Śāriputra, very deep sūtras connected with the six perfections will indeed appear to those sons of good family and daughters of good family."
Śāriputra said:
"Lord, for which sons of good family and daughters of good family will they arise?
The Blessed One replied:

"Śāriputra, those bodhisattvas, sons of good family, and daughters of good family who, for the sake of these six perfections, shall apply themselves with intense faith, regardless of body or life— for what reason is this so?
It is because it is thus, Śāriputra."
Those who establish beings in unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, who demonstrate it to them, who encourage them,

who inspire them, who gladden them, and who settle them therein— Śāriputra, for those sons of good family and daughters of good family, even when they have passed away from that birth, these six perfections will arise once more.

Engaging in those six perfections as they have been taught, they will not rely upon such vigor until they have purified the buddha-field, matured sentient beings, and awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Thus, the qualities of the perfection of wisdom have been described as the quality of attaining certainty through the reversal of non-greed and the absence of the conceptualization of greed.
Then the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:

"Blessed One, these qualities have been proclaimed for those sons of good family and daughters of good family who have set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, who will practice the six perfections,
and who will bring sentient beings to maturity."
They will purify the Buddha-fields. "But, Blessed One, what kind of obstacles will arise for those sons of good family and daughters of good family?
The Blessed One said:
"Their eloquence will arise after a long time."
"Subhūti, this should be understood as the work of Māra for bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas.
Subhūti said:
"For what reason, Blessed One, will the inspired eloquence arise only after a long time?"
"What should be understood as the work of Māra for bodhisattvas, the great beings?
The Blessed One said:

"In this regard, Subhūti, a bodhisattva, a great being, while practicing the perfection of wisdom, will fulfill the perfection of wisdom with difficulty; he will fulfill the perfection of meditation with difficulty."
With difficulty he will fulfill the perfection of vigor; with difficulty he will fulfill the perfection of patience;
with difficulty he will fulfill the perfection of ethical discipline.
He will fulfill the perfection of generosity only with great difficulty;
Subhūti, by this method, his eloquence will arise after a long time.
Subhūti, this should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. Thus ends the attainment of difficulty.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, if inspired eloquence should arise very rapidly and he should think [he has attained it],
this too, Subhūti, should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas.
Subhūti said:
"In what manner, Blessed One, does the work of Māra arise through the too-quick arising of inspired eloquence in Bodhisattvas, Mahāsattvas?
The Blessed One said:

"In this case, Subhūti, for a Bodhisattva, Mahāsattva who practices the perfection of giving, and who practices the perfections of morality, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom, but who lacks skill in means, there arises too-quick..."

"Subhūti, by this method, one should recognize as the work of Māra the arising of inspired eloquence too quickly for Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas. Furthermore, Subhūti, when they yawn while writing this Perfection of Wisdom, there will be an arising of inspired eloquence."
This too, Subhūti, should be understood as a work of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, Subhūti, they will write down this perfection of wisdom while laughing;
this too, Subhūti, should be understood as a work of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, Subhūti, they will write down this perfection of wisdom while mocking one another;
Subhūti, this too should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. Thus, there are three kinds of physical corruption and depravity.
Furthermore, Subhūti, they will write it down with distracted minds.
Subhūti, this too should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, Subhūti, they will write it down while possessing mutual consciousness;
Subhūti, this too should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, Subhūti, it will occur to some bodhisattva mahāsattvas:
"We do not find any taste in this," and they will rise from their seats and depart.
Subhūti, this too should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. Thus, there are three kinds of mental corruption.
Furthermore, Subhūti, yawning and rising from their seats, they will depart;
this too, Subhūti, should be known as a work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, Subhūti, yawning, they will study, retain, recite, and teach [the teachings].
If they yawn while attending to it, Subhūti, this too should be known as a work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, Subhūti, if they take up, retain, recite, and master [this] while laughing with one another, [this too is a work of Māra].
If they laugh at one another while attending to it properly, Subhūti, this too should be known as a work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, Subhūti, if they write it down, take it up, bear it in mind, recite it, master it, and attend to it properly while mocking one another, [this too is a work of Māra].
This too, Subhūti, should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas.

Furthermore, Subhūti, if they will take it up, retain it, recite it, master it, and attend to it properly with distracted minds, this too, Subhūti, should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas.
"Furthermore, Subhūti, there will be those who, possessing mutual physical charms, will take up, retain, recite, master, and properly attend to [this teaching].

Subhūti, this too should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. When this had been said—referring to the lack of application in recitation and so forth—the venerable Subhūti addressed the Blessed One as follows:
"Venerable Lord, when they say, 'We do not find any relish in this,' and rise from their seats and depart,
this too, Subhūti, should be understood as a work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. "For what reason, Venerable Lord, do they not find any relish in this?"

The Blessed One said: "For indeed, Subhūti, they have not previously practiced the perfection of wisdom, nor the perfection of meditation, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of patience, or the perfection of ethical discipline."
For it is thus, Subhūti: because they did not previously practice the perfection of generosity,
for that reason, Subhūti, they do not find any relish in this perfection of wisdom.
While this is being spoken, they will rise from their seats and depart.

Furthermore, Subhūti, it occurs to some bodhisattva mahāsattvas: "We have not been prophesied here regarding the perfection of wisdom. With such a lack of serene confidence, they will rise from their seats and depart.
"Subhūti, this too should be understood as a work of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas.
Subhūti said:
"For what reason, Blessed One, will those who have not been prophesied depart from their seats and leave, having failed to rise up in the perfection of wisdom?"
The Blessed One said:
"Furthermore, Subhūti, bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have not yet entered into the fixed course of certainty are not prophesied for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment;
they will not gain faith here because they think, 'My name has not been mentioned in this Perfection of Wisdom.'"
"Subhūti, this too should be understood as a work of Māra for bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas.
Subhūti said:
"For what reason, Blessed One, are the names of the bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas not proclaimed here in this profound perfection of wisdom?"
The Blessed One said:

"Furthermore, Subhūti, the names of those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have not been prophesied are not proclaimed; nor is my name proclaimed, nor the name of the village, city, town, capital, or kingdom where I was born."
He will think that the perfection of wisdom is not to be heard;
he will think that he must depart from that assembly;
and the more he thinks he must depart, the further he will become from the qualities of a Buddha.
For as many eons as they shall generate the production of the thought of awakening through their application, for that long he will sustain them,
wherein he must once again apply himself to yoga.

They will consider those sūtras to be sought after because they grasp at signs of aversion; thus, having abandoned the perfection of wisdom—which brings about the knowledge of omniscience—they will consider those [other sūtras] to be what must be sought.
In this way, sons of good family and daughters of good family [will fail] in the attainment of the knowledge of omniscience.
"Subhūti, they will think that one should discard the root and instead rely upon the branches, leaves, and foliage;
this too, Subhūti, should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
Subhūti said:
“Blessed One, which are those sūtras that do not bring about the knowledge of omniscience, yet which they will think ought to be mastered?
The Blessed One said:

Those discourses associated with the vehicle of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas— namely, the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the branches of awakening, and the path; as well as the gateways to liberation consisting of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness— by abiding in which sons and daughters of good family attain the fruit of stream-entry.
They attain the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, arhatship, and pratyekabuddha-enlightenment;
Subhūti, these are the discourses associated with the levels of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas,
which do not lead to the attainment of omniscience.
Having abandoned the perfection of wisdom, they will think that [other teachings] are what should be mastered. Why is that?
Subhūti, it is because Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas are born from the perfection of wisdom and shall go forth by means of mundane and supramundane dharmas;
Subhūti, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas train in the perfection of wisdom, they will train in mundane and supramundane dharmas. Thus is the failure of the cause.

Subhūti, it is just as if a dog, having rejected a morsel from its master, should think that it must seek a mouthful from a servant. In the same way, Subhūti, there will be in the future time sons of good family and daughters of good family belonging to the Mahāyāna who [will reject] this profound perfection of wisdom, the root of all the qualities of a Buddha.

Having cast aside those discourses associated with the vehicle of the śrāvakas and those associated with the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas— which are like branches, leaves, and foliage— they will consider [only those] to be what should be mastered.
Subhūti, this too should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, Subhūti, in the future time there will be sons of good family and daughters of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle who,

having abandoned this profound perfection of wisdom, will think that those teachings associated with the vehicles of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas are what they should master for the sake of gain and honor.
Subhūti, this too should be known as a work of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas: namely, the loss of the taste for what is sublime.
Subhūti, it is just as if some man were in need of an elephant;
having obtained an elephant, he might think that he must search for the footprint of an elephant. What do you think?
"Subhūti, would that man be considered wise?
Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One."
The Blessed One said:

"Subhūti, it should be understood that it is exactly the same for those persons belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle who, having abandoned this profound perfection of wisdom, [take up] those discourses associated with the vehicle of the śrāvakas or associated with the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas."
They will think that those [perfections] are what must be mastered. What do you think, Subhūti?
Would those sons of good family and daughters of good family belonging to the Mahāyāna be of a wise nature?
Subhūti replied:
"No, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
"Subhūti, this too is a work of Māra for bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas."
It should be understood that this is the non-falling away from the supreme vehicle.
Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, a man should desire to see the great ocean,
and having seen the great ocean, he should think that he must search for a cow’s footprint.
Having seen that single footprint of a cow, he would think, "The great ocean is of such a measure. What do you think, Subhūti?
Would that man be considered wise?
Subhūti said: "No, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:

In the same way, Subhūti, those sons of good family and daughters of good family belonging to the Great Vehicle should be understood as being of such a nature, who, having heard or obtained this perfection of wisdom, would reject it and think that the discourses associated with the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas are what should be taken up. What do you think, Subhūti?
Would those sons of good family and daughters of good family belonging to the Great Vehicle be of a wise disposition?
Subhūti said: "No, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
"Subhūti, this too should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas: namely, the failure of the summary.

Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, a carpenter or a carpenter’s apprentice, desiring to build a palace equal in size to the Vaijayanta Palace, should think that he must take the measurements from the celestial mansions of the disks of the sun and the moon. What do you think?"
"Subhūti, suppose someone, desiring to build a palace equal to the Vaijayanta [palace], were to take the measurements from the celestial mansions of the sun and moon;
would that person be considered wise?
Subhūti replied:
"No, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
"In the same way, Subhūti, in a future time there will be certain sons of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle."

And as for those daughters of good family who, having heard or obtained this profound perfection of wisdom, should abandon or discard it and think that omniscience is to be sought through discourses associated with the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas— what do you think about that?
"Subhūti, would those bodhisattvas, sons of good family, and daughters of good family be considered wise?
Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One."
The Blessed One said:

"Subhūti, this too should be known as a work of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas; namely, the failure to understand the connection between cause and fruit. Furthermore, Subhūti, it is just as if some man, having seen a local king, were to think thus:"

"A universal monarch is such in complexion and physical form as this local king here. Having grasped the signs, marks, and characteristics of the local king's complexion, physical form, and appearance, he might say, "Such is the specific excellence of complexion, physical form, and appearance of a universal monarch. What do you think?
"Subhūti, would that man be considered wise?
Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One."
The Blessed One said:
"In the same way, Subhūti, in a future time there will be certain sons of good family and daughters of good family belonging to the Mahāyāna who,
having heard or obtained this profound perfection of wisdom, will neglect it or cast it aside."

They will think that omniscience (sarvākārajñatā) is to be sought through the discourses associated with the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas. What do you think, Subhūti, would those sons of good family and daughters of good family belonging to the Mahāyāna be of a wise nature?
Subhūti said:
"No, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
"Subhūti, this too should be known as a work of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas. Thus is the falling away from the unsurpassed state."

Furthermore, Subhūti, many flashes of inspired eloquence will arise for those sons of good family and daughters of good family who write down this perfection of wisdom, which will distract them while they are writing this profound perfection of wisdom. They will be like flashes of inspired eloquence regarding form, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and mental phenomena; or flashes of inspired eloquence regarding the perfection of generosity, and flashes of inspired eloquence regarding the perfections of ethical discipline, patience, vigor, meditative concentration, and wisdom.

The eloquence regarding the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm; the eloquence regarding recitation and study; the eloquence regarding service; the eloquence regarding the foundations of mindfulness; the eloquence regarding the right efforts; the eloquence regarding the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the path;
the eloquence regarding all meditations, liberations, concentrations, attainments, and doors of dhāraṇī; and the eloquence regarding internal emptiness.

the manifestation of external emptiness, the manifestation of internal-external emptiness, the manifestation of the emptiness of emptiness, the manifestation of great emptiness, the manifestation of ultimate emptiness, the manifestation of conditioned emptiness, the manifestation of unconditioned emptiness, and the manifestation of absolute emptiness;

Up to the eloquence of the emptiness of the nature of non-existence, the eloquence of the powers, the eloquence of the fearlessnesses, the eloquence of the analytical knowledges and the unique qualities of a Buddha, up to the eloquence of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening. For what reason?
Subhūti, it is because the perfection of wisdom is indeed non-eloquence.
For the perfection of wisdom, Subhūti, is inconceivable; for the perfection of wisdom, Subhūti, is beyond thought and free from the inconceivable;
for the perfection of wisdom, Subhūti, is without arising and without cessation.
For, Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is neither afflicted nor purified;
for, Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is non-distraction;
for, Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is ineffable.
For, Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is free from ill-will;
for, Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is non-apprehensible. Why is that?
Because, Subhūti, these phenomena do not exist within this profound perfection of wisdom. If, Subhūti...
“Subhūti, when a son of good family or a daughter of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle hears this profound perfection of wisdom,

if their attention is distracted by the act of writing it down, this too, Subhūti, should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas. Thus, there is the arising of the manifestation of conceptualizations regarding various objects.”
Subhūti said:
"But, Blessed One, is it possible to write down the perfection of wisdom?
The Blessed One said: "No, Subhūti."
For what reason?
Subhūti, the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom does not exist;
nor does the intrinsic nature of the perfection of meditation, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of patience, the perfection of ethical discipline, or the perfection of generosity exist.

The intrinsic nature of all the emptinesses does not exist; nor does the intrinsic nature of the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, nor of the noble truths, exist; nor does the intrinsic nature of the immeasurables, the meditative absorptions, or the formless attainments exist; nor does the intrinsic nature of emptiness, signlessness, or wishlessness exist; nor does the intrinsic nature of the eight liberations or the nine successive meditative attainments exist; nor does the intrinsic nature of the superknowledges exist; nor do the intrinsic natures of all the samādhis or all the doors of dhāraṇī exist.
The intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) of the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha does not exist;

nor does the intrinsic nature of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) exist. That which has no intrinsic nature is non-existence (*abhāva*); and that which is non-existence is this very perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). Yet, non-existence cannot be written down by means of non-existence.
Thus, attachment to writing is an obstacle.

Furthermore, Subhūti, if sons of good family or daughters of good family belonging to the Mahāyāna should perceive this perfection of wisdom as "non-existence," this too should be known as their work of Māra;
thus, attachment to non-existence is an obstacle.
Subhūti said:

"Blessed One, whatever sons of good family or daughters of good family belonging to the Mahāyāna shall write down this profound perfection of wisdom in written letters and think, 'I have written down the profound perfection of wisdom,'"
"They will also become attached to this profound *prajñāpāramitā* within the scripts and letters;
O Blessed One, this too should be known as their work of Māra. Thus, Subhūti spoke regarding the obstacle of attachment to the *prajñāpāramitā* within scripts and letters.
For what reason?
Because, Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is indeed without letters,
and the perfection of meditation is indeed without letters.
For the perfection of vigor is indeed without letters; for the perfection of patience is indeed without letters;
for the perfection of ethical discipline is indeed without letters.
For the perfection of generosity is indeed without syllables;
O Blessed One, form is without syllables,
as are feeling, perception, and mental formations.
"Blessed One, consciousness is without syllables; Blessed One, the elements are without syllables;
Blessed One, the sense bases are without syllables."
Blessed One, dependent origination is without syllables; the factors of dependent origination are without syllables;
the thirty-seven factors conducive to enlightenment are without syllables.
All emptinesses are without syllables; all samādhis are without syllables;
all doors of dhāraṇī are without syllables.
All emptinesses, signs, and wishlessnesses are without letters;
the noble truths are without letters;
all the immeasurables, meditative absorptions, and formless attainments are without letters.
The eight liberations are without syllables; the nine successive meditative attainments are without syllables;
the superknowledges are without syllables.
The powers of a Tathāgata are beyond syllables; the grounds of self-confidence are beyond syllables;
the analytical knowledges are beyond syllables.
The eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are beyond letters,
for omniscience itself, O Blessed One, is beyond letters.

Furthermore, O Blessed One, if sons of good family or daughters of good family belonging to the Mahāyāna should adhere to the perfection of wisdom as being beyond letters, [they would not truly understand it].
In this way, they will adhere to the perfection of meditation, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of patience, and the perfection of ethical discipline;
they will adhere to the letterless perfection of generosity. They will adhere to form as being letterless, and likewise to sensation, perception, and mental formations.

They will adhere to consciousness as being without syllables. In this same way, they will adhere to the aggregates, elements, sense bases, dependent origination, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment,
the gates of liberation, the truths, the immeasurables, the meditative concentrations, the formless attainments, the powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges,
and the unique qualities of a Buddha as being without syllables.
"Up until they become attached to omniscience as being without letters—this too, Blessed One, should be known as a work of Māra for those bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas.
Thus, in the *Prajñāpāramitā*, there is an obstacle consisting of attachment to the letterless.
Furthermore, Subhūti, as these sons of good family and daughters of good family write down this *Prajñāpāramitā*, discursive thoughts concerning their native lands will arise."
This too, Subhūti, should be known as a work of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas.

Furthermore, Subhūti, for those sons of good family and daughters of good family belonging to the Mahāyāna who are writing out this profound perfection of wisdom, there will arise mental preoccupations with villages, mental preoccupations with cities, and mental preoccupations with market towns.
Mental engagements with the royal capital, mental engagements with the kingdom, mental engagements with the gods, mental engagements with teachers and preceptors,
mental engagements associated with mother, father, brothers, sisters, sons, daughters, and kinsmen,
and mental engagements with thieves.

Mental engagements associated with outcasts, mental engagements associated with sensual thoughts, and mental engagements associated with socializing will arise. Subhūti, these and many other various kinds of mental engagements of bodhisattva mahāsattvas should be understood as the work of Māra. This—

Māra, the Evil One, will bring about obstacles and distractions for those who write down, point out, recite, and properly attend to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*. Thus ends the obstacle of mental attention directed toward [secular] districts and so forth.
Furthermore, Subhūti, for these sons of good family and daughters of good family, bodhisattvas who write down, point out, recite, and properly attend to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*...

Those sons of good family and daughters of good family who are bodhisattvas, relishing gain, honor, praise, and the requisites of robes, alms-food, lodgings, and medicinal provisions for the sick, will write down this profound perfection of wisdom, teach it, recite it, and attend to it with wise reflection. Subhūti, this too should be understood as a work of Māra against the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas.

Thus, Subhūti, gain, honor, and the taste for fame are obstacles; furthermore, Māra the Evil One will bring forth to those bodhisattvas mahāsattvas various very profound sūtras, [intending] those who are writing down this profound perfection of wisdom, teaching it, reciting it, and attending to it with wise reflection.
Furthermore, Subhūti, bodhisattvas who are skilled in means should not give rise to a longing for those extremely profound sūtras that have been brought forth by Māra. Why is that?
Because, Subhūti, those sūtras do not bring about omniscience. In this regard, Subhūti, those who are unskilled in means...
There will be bodhisattvas who, having heard this profound perfection of wisdom, will abandon it—

wherein the skillful means of bodhisattva mahāsattvas have been explained by me in detail— and wherein this very profound perfection of wisdom, in which skillful means is to be sought in detail. Furthermore, Subhūti, those followers of the Great Vehicle...

"O sons of good family or daughters of good family, having abandoned this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, they will think that skill in means (*upāyakauśalya*) is to be sought from those discourses associated with the vehicles of the *śrāvakas* and *pratyekabuddhas*. Subhūti, this too should be known as a work of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas; it is an obstacle consisting in the search for the path of skill in means by way of a non-path."

Furthermore, Subhūti, there will be those who desire to write, teach, recite, and study the *prajñāpāramitā*, yet the Dharma-preacher will be indolent. This too, Subhūti, should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas; this is the discordance arising from desire and indolence.
Furthermore, Subhūti, the Dharma-preacher may be free from indolence regarding this [perfection].

To cause the profound *prajñāpāramitā* to be written down, taken up, taught, and recited, there will be listeners of the Dharma who have set out for other regions. Subhūti, this too should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, Subhūti, there will be listeners of the Dharma who desire to write down the *prajñāpāramitā*, who desire to take it up, who desire to teach it, and who desire to recite it.

Furthermore, Subhūti, the Dharma-preacher will have set out for another country. This also, Subhūti, should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. Thus is the failure of the object due to the breaking of desire.
Moreover, Subhūti, the Dharma-preacher will be one who values gain, honor, and praise; he will be attached to the requisites of robes, alms-food, lodgings, and medicinal supplies for the sick.
Furthermore, Subhūti, those who listen to the Dharma may have few desires, be contented, exerted in vigor, established in mindfulness, concentrated, single-minded,

and possessed of wisdom. Even this, Subhūti, should be understood as a work of Māra for Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas when the Prajñāpāramitā is being written down, recited, or properly attended to with right mental attention, due to such a lack of harmony.
Furthermore, Subhūti, the Dharma-preacher will be one who has few desires, is contented, secluded, energetic, established in mindfulness, concentrated, single-minded, and possessed of wisdom;

yet the listeners of the Dharma will have great desires, evil desires, and will value gain, honor, and fame, as well as robes, alms-food, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick. This too, Subhūti, is a lack of harmony when the Prajñāpāramitā is being written or recited.
When this is being attended to through wise reflection, it should be understood as the work of Māra for Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
Thus, there is the failure of fewness of wishes due to the weightiness of gain.
Furthermore, Subhūti, a Dharma-preacher will be a forest-dweller, yet...

They will be alms-food eaters, wearers of rag-robes, those who refuse food after the proper time, those who eat at a single sitting, those who accept only a bowlful of food, those who dwell in cemeteries, those who dwell in the open air, those who dwell at the foot of trees, those who remain in a sitting posture, and those who accept whatever bedding is offered; yet they will not be forest-dwellers, nor will they be alms-food eaters, nor wearers of rag-robes, nor those who refuse food after the proper time,

nor those who eat at a single sitting, nor those who accept only a bowlful of food, nor those who dwell in cemeteries, nor those who dwell in the open air, nor those who dwell at the foot of trees, nor those who remain in a sitting posture.
They do not practice the vow of sleeping wherever one lies down, nor do they observe the vow of possessing only three robes. Subhūti,

this too should be known as the work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas when this profound perfection of wisdom is being written, taught, recited, or properly attended to with right mental focus, due to a lack of concord.

Furthermore, Subhūti, there will be a listener of the Dharma who is a forest-dweller, and so on, up to one who possesses only the three robes; yet the preacher of the Dharma will not be a forest-dweller, nor will he possess the three robes. This too, Subhūti, is a lack of harmony when this profound perfection of wisdom is being written down, taught, or recited with proper attention.
And when this is being attended to, it should be understood as the work of Māra for the bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
Thus, there is a lack of application to the practice of the ascetic virtues (dhūtaguṇa).

Furthermore, Subhūti, there will be listeners of the Dharma who are faithful and possessed of wholesome qualities, desiring to write down this profound perfection of wisdom, desiring to teach it, and desiring to recite it.

Furthermore, Subhūti, the Dharma-preacher will be without faith and lacking in virtuous qualities; he will have no desire to write down this profound perfection of wisdom, no desire to teach it, and no desire to recite it. This also, Subhūti, should be recognized as a work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas.

Furthermore, Subhūti, there will be a Dharma-preacher who is faithful and possesses virtuous qualities, desiring to write and give this profound *prajñāpāramitā* to one who seeks it and desires to receive it;

yet the listener of the Dharma will be faithless and lack virtuous qualities, not desiring to write or give this profound *prajñāpāramitā* to one who seeks it, nor desiring to teach it or have it received. This too, Subhūti, [is a difficulty] for bodhisattvas.
This should be understood as the work of Māra for great beings.
Thus is the deficiency of desiring what is wholesome and unwholesome.
Furthermore, Subhūti, the Dharma-preacher will be one who relinquishes all possessions and possesses a mind free from grasping.

Furthermore, Subhūti, the one who listens to the Dharma will be envious, full of great desire, and possessed of evil desires; he will be preoccupied with gain, honor, fame, robes, alms-food, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick. This too, Subhūti, should be known as the work of Māra against those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who write down, teach, and recite this profound Perfection of Wisdom, due to a lack of harmony.
Furthermore, Subhūti, there will be a case where the listener of the Dharma will be one who has renounced all possessions and possesses a mind free from grasping,

while the preacher of the Dharma will be stingy and miserly. This too, Subhūti, is a lack of harmony for those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who are writing down, teaching, or reciting this profound perfection of wisdom.

This should be known as the work of Māra. Furthermore, Subhūti, there will be a lack of generosity and an abundance of stinginess; the listener of the Dharma will desire to give away robes, alms-food, bowls, bedding, seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick to the preacher of the Dharma, yet the preacher of the Dharma will not wish to accept them. This too, Subhūti, will be a lack of harmony.

Subhūti, when this profound perfection of wisdom is being written down, taught, recited, or properly attended to with right reflection, this too should be recognized as a deed of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. Furthermore, Subhūti, there will be a Dharma-preacher who desires to receive [offerings] from the presence of a listener of the Dharma.

And the listener of the Dharma will not be desirous of giving. This too, Subhūti, will be a lack of harmony when this profound perfection of wisdom is being written down, taught, recited, or properly attended to with right mental attention. This also, Subhūti, should be understood as a work of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas.
Thus there will be a lack of both giving and receiving.

Furthermore, Subhūti, the Dharma-preacher will be one who understands through brief explanations, while the listener of the Dharma will be one who requires detailed exposition, or one who understands through elaboration, or one for whom the words alone are paramount. This too, Subhūti, will be a lack of harmony.
Subhūti, this too should be understood as a work of Māra for those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who write down, teach, or recite this profound *prajñāpāramitā*.

Furthermore, Subhūti, the listener of the Dharma may be one who understands through concise explanations (*udghaṭitajña*), while the preacher of the Dharma may be one who requires detailed exposition (*vipañcitajña*), or one who relies solely on the literal words (*padaparama*). Subhūti, this too will be a lack of harmony.

Subhūti, this too should be known as a work of Māra for those bodhisattva mahāsattvas who write down, point out, recite, and attend to this profound *prajñāpāramitā*. This refers to the deficiency in being one who knows by a mere summary or one who knows through detailed exposition. Furthermore, Subhūti, the Dharma-preacher may know other teachings—sūtras, geyas, vyākaraṇas, gāthās, udānas, avadānas, itivṛttakas, jātakas, nidānas, vaipulyas, adbhutadharmas, and upadeśas—[but not this].

Furthermore, Subhūti, those who listen to the Dharma will not understand other teachings— namely, the discourses (*sūtra*), mixed prose and verse (*geya*), prophecies (*vyākaraṇa*), verses (*gāthā*), inspired utterances (*udāna*), legends (*avadāna*), historical narratives (*itivṛttaka*), birth stories (*jātaka*), introductory accounts (*nidāna*), extensive treatises (*vaipulya*), marvelous events (*adbhutadharma*), and instructions (*upadeśa*). This too, Subhūti, will be a lack of concord when this profound perfection of wisdom is being written down, taught, and recited.
Subhūti, when this is being attended to, this too should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. Furthermore, Subhūti,

it may be that the listener of the Dharma understands one category of the Dharma— namely, the discourses (*sūtra*), songs (*geya*), prophecies (*vyākaraṇa*), verses (*gāthā*), inspired utterances (*udāna*), legends (*avadāna*), past events (*itivṛttaka*), birth stories (*jātaka*), causal narratives (*nidāna*), extensive teachings (*vaipulya*), marvelous qualities (*adbhutadharma*), and instructions (*upadeśa*)— while the preacher of the Dharma does not understand another category of the Dharma, namely, the discourses, songs, prophecies, verses, inspired utterances, legends, past events, birth stories, causal narratives, extensive teachings, marvelous qualities, and instructions.

Subhūti, this too will be a lack of harmony when this profound perfection of wisdom is being written down, taught, recited, or attended to. Subhūti, this also should be understood as a work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
Thus, there will be a deficiency in the mastery and non-mastery of the dharmas such as the sūtras.
Furthermore, Subhūti, the Dharma-preacher will be endowed with the six perfections,
but the listener of the Dharma will not be endowed with the six perfections.

Subhūti, this too will be a lack of harmony for those who write down, teach, recite, and attend to this profound perfection of wisdom. Subhūti, this also should be known as the work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, Subhūti, there will be listeners of the Dharma who are endowed with the six perfections.

And the Dharma-preacher will not be endowed with the six perfections. This too, Subhūti, will be a lack of harmony for those who write down, teach, recite, or attend to this profound perfection of wisdom. This also, Subhūti, should be understood as a work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. Thus [ends] the deficiency regarding the possession or non-possession of the six perfections.

Furthermore, Subhūti, the Dharma-preacher will be skilled in means regarding the six perfections, while the listeners of the Dharma will be unskilled in means regarding the six perfections. This too, Subhūti, will be a lack of harmony when this profound perfection of wisdom is being written down, taught, recited, and attended to. This also, Subhūti, [is an obstacle] for the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas...
This should be understood as the work of Māra.
Furthermore, Subhūti, the listeners of the Dharma will be skillful in means regarding the six perfections,
while the preacher of the Dharma will be unskillful in means regarding the six perfections.
Subhūti, this too will be a lack of harmony when this profound *prajñāpāramitā* is being written down, taught, recited, or attended to with mental attention.
Subhūti, this also should be known as a work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas; namely, the deficiency in skill regarding means and non-means.
Furthermore, Subhūti, the Dharma-preacher will have attained dhāraṇī,
whereas the listeners of the Dharma will not have attained dhāraṇī; this too, Subhūti, will be a lack of harmony.

Subhūti, when this profound *prajñāpāramitā* is being written down, taught, recited, or attended to with the mind, this too should be understood as a work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas; namely, the failure to attain the *dhāraṇī*. This is the deficiency regarding the non-attainment of the *dhāraṇī*.

Furthermore, Subhūti, there will be a case where the Dharma-preacher desires to write it down, desires to retain it, desires to recite it, desires to study it, and even desires to attend to it with the mind,
yet the listeners of the Dharma do not desire to write it down, nor do they desire to attend to it with the mind;
this too, Subhūti, will be a lack of harmony.
Subhūti, this too should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas who write out, recite, or even cultivate this profound *prajñāpāramitā*.
Furthermore, Subhūti, there will be those who wish to hear the Dharma, wishing to write it out, and so on, up to wishing to attend to it mentally;
yet the Dharma-preacher will not wish to write it out, nor wish to attend to it mentally.

Subhūti, this too will be a lack of harmony for those who write, recite, or even cultivate this profound perfection of wisdom. Subhūti, this also should be known as a work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
Thus ends the section on the failure of the desire to write.
Furthermore, Subhūti, the Dharma-preacher will be free from sensual desire, ill-will, sloth and torpor, restlessness and remorse, and doubt;
and the listeners of the Dharma will also be free from sensual desire, ill-will, sloth and torpor, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.
This too, Subhūti, will be a lack of harmony.

Subhūti, this too should be known as a work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas who desire to write down this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, up to those who desire to cultivate it. Furthermore, Subhūti, the listeners of the Dharma will be free from sensual desire, ill-will, sloth and torpor, restlessness and remorse, and doubt,
while the teacher of the Dharma will not be free from sensual desire, ill-will, sloth and torpor, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.
Subhūti, this too will be a lack of harmony for those who wish to write down this profound perfection of wisdom, up to those who wish to cultivate it.
Subhūti, this also should be recognized as a work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas.

Thus, Subhūti, for those who— free from the affliction of sensual desire and other such hindrances— are writing this profound perfection of wisdom, up to and including practicing it, someone may come there and speak dispraise of the hells, speak dispraise of the animal realm, or speak dispraise of the hungry ghosts.
"The hells are thus full of suffering, the animal realm is thus full of suffering, and the sphere of hungry ghosts is thus full of suffering;
therefore, put an end to suffering right here! Why do you seek to realize unexcelled, perfect enlightenment? Subhūti, this too will be a lack of harmony there.

Subhūti, this too should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas who write down this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, up to and including those who cultivate it. This refers to their turning away from the states of miserable rebirth.

Furthermore, Subhūti, while they are writing down this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, up to and including attending to it with proper mental attention, someone may come and speak in praise of the gods of the Four Great Kings, up to and including those who have reached the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
He will speak in praise of the gods: "Thus is the realm of desire pleasant through the enjoyment of sensual pleasures;
thus is the realm of form pleasant through meditative absorptions and attainments; thus is the formless realm pleasant through its states of peace."
All that, too, is impermanent, suffering, empty, and without self; it is subject to transformation, subject to decay, subject to dispassion, and subject to cessation.
Right here, you should attain the fruit of stream-entry; attain the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and arhatship; attain solitary enlightenment;
do not wander for a long time in saṃsāra.
This too, Subhūti, should be understood as a deed of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, Subhūti, there will be a Dharma-preacher who is alone and without a companion, acting by himself, yet he will feel joy at the prospect of going to a happy rebirth.
Furthermore, Subhūti, the one who listens to the Dharma will wander among the assemblies;

this too will be a lack of harmony for those writing, reciting, or studying this profound perfection of wisdom. Subhūti, this also should be understood as the work of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, Subhūti, there will be a listener of the Dharma who is solitary and acts alone,
while the preacher of the Dharma will frequent assemblies; this too, Subhūti, will be a lack of harmony.

Subhūti, this too should be known as a work of Māra for Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who write, recite, or study this profound *prajñāpāramitā*. Thus, there is the deficiency of wandering alone rather than in a group.
Furthermore, Subhūti, the Dharma-preacher will say: "Whoever follows me..."
I shall give this perfection of wisdom to him for the purpose of writing it down, reciting it, teaching it, studying it, attending to it, and cultivating it;
and he will not be followed by one who merely listens to the Dharma.

Subhūti, this too will be a lack of harmony when this profound perfection of wisdom is being written down, spoken, recited, or studied. Furthermore, Subhūti, this too will be another [obstacle] for bodhisattva mahāsattvas: that the listener of the Dharma will desire to follow after the preacher of the Dharma.
Furthermore, Subhūti, the Dharma-preacher will not grant an opportunity for [the listener] to follow after him;
this too will be a lack of harmony there when this profound perfection of wisdom is being written down, spoken, recited, or studied.
Subhūti, this too should be known as a work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. That is, the deficiency caused by not granting an opportunity because one desires to follow after [the teacher].
Furthermore, Subhūti, a Dharma-preacher may desire to give this perfection of wisdom—for the sake of writing it down, teaching it, or even practicing it—for the sake of some small material gain.
Furthermore, Subhūti, the listener of the Dharma will not be inclined to approach for the sake of even a small amount of material gain;
this too, Subhūti, will be a lack of harmony there while this profound perfection of wisdom is being written down, up to its being cultivated.
This too, Subhūti, should be understood as a deed of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas.
Thus is the deficiency of not wishing to give even a small amount of material things.
Furthermore, Subhūti, the Dharma-preacher will desire to go to those regions, [while the listener remains behind].
In whichever direction there will be an obstacle to life,
and the listener of the Dharma has no desire to go to that place—
Subhūti, this too will be a lack of harmony.
Subhūti, while this profound perfection of wisdom is being written down, taught, recited, attended to, and cultivated,
this too should be understood as a work of Māra against the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas. Furthermore, Subhūti, there will be a listener of the Dharma who desires to go to those regions.
Subhūti, in whichever direction there will be a threat to life, and the Dharma-preacher has no desire to go to that place—
this too, Subhūti, will be a lack of harmony.
Subhūti, while this profound *prajñāpāramitā* is being written down, and so on, up to being cultivated,
this too should be understood as a work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas:
namely, obstacles to life, and the failure to proceed or return in the various directions.
Furthermore, Subhūti, it may happen that the Dharma-preacher wishes to go where there is famine and lack of water,
while the listener of the Dharma has no desire to go there.
Subhūti, this too will be a lack of harmony while this profound perfection of wisdom is being written down, up to its being cultivated.
This too, Subhūti, should be known as a work of Māra for bodhisattvas mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, Subhūti, the Dharma-preacher will go to where there is good food and plenty of water.
And those who come to hear the Dharma will follow him, and he will say to them:
"Noble sons, have you well-considered going there for the sake of material gain? Do not later become regretful regarding the alms-food you have obtained or failed to obtain."
In this way, that Dharma-preacher will have rejected the Dharma through subtle means;
they, appearing despondent, will think, "These are signs of rejection, not signs of a desire to give.
Subhūti, this too will be a lack of harmony.
Subhūti, when this profound *prajñāpāramitā* is being written down, taught, recited, spoken, or cultivated,
this too should be recognized as a work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas: namely,
the frustration caused by the inability to travel to or from regions where there is famine or abundance.

Furthermore, Subhūti, the monk who is the Dharma-preacher will set out toward where there is danger from thieves, danger from outcasts, danger from hunters, danger from fierce beasts, danger from venomous serpents,
danger from wildernesses and forests, and danger from difficult passes; and these listeners of the Dharma will likewise desire to hear this profound perfection of wisdom.
They will follow after the Dharma-preacher,

and that Dharma-preaching monk will say to them: "Noble sons, why would you go to a place where there is fear of thieves, fear of outcasts, fear of hunters, fear of fierce wild beasts, fear of venomous serpents, fear of wildernesses and forests, and fear of difficult terrain?"
Furthermore, those listeners of the Dharma who desire to hear this profound perfection of wisdom will follow after the Dharma-preacher;
yet that Dharma-preacher monk will have no desire to speak it,
no desire to have this profound perfection of wisdom written down, no desire to recite it, and no desire to cause others to hear it.
Having heard it from that Dharma-preacher, being filled with disillusionment, they will not go where that Dharma-preaching monk goes;
this too, Subhūti, will be a lack of concord while this profound perfection of wisdom is being written down, up to its being cultivated.
Subhūti, this too should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas.

Furthermore, Subhūti, there will be a Dharma-preaching monk who becomes preoccupied with families that provide alms; because of that preoccupation with families providing alms, he will think that those families must be visited frequently, and by that frequent visiting of families—
He will refuse those who come to hear the Dharma,
saying, "Venerable ones, there are families from whom I must not look for alms and to which I must go";
thus he will refuse those seekers of the Dharma, and being refused, they will turn back.
Subhūti, this too will be a lack of harmony for those who write, cultivate, teach, or recite the *prajñāpāramitā*.
Subhūti, this also should be known as a work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
Thus ends the deficiency regarding the examination of family.

"Furthermore, Subhūti, Māra the Evil One will act in the guise of a monk through various means, by whatever means possible, so that no one at all shall write down this perfection of wisdom, nor take it up, nor master it, nor retain it, nor recite it, nor study it, nor attend to it with the mind. When this was said, the venerable Subhūti addressed the Blessed One as follows:
For what reason, Blessed One, will Māra the Evil One act in such and such a manner in the guise of a monk,
so that no one at all will write down this profound perfection of wisdom, nor take it up, nor master it, nor retain it, nor recite it, nor study it, nor attend to it with the mind?
The Blessed One said:

"For the abandonments of the afflictions of all sentient beings are born from the perfection of wisdom; therefore, he will act by such and such means so that no one at all will write down this profound perfection of wisdom, nor take it up, nor master it."
He will not uphold it, nor recite it, nor study it, nor attend to it in his mind.
Furthermore, Subhūti, Māra, the Evil One, having approached in the guise of a monk, will sow discord and cause division, saying:
"This is not the Perfection of Wisdom; it does not accord with the sūtra as it has come down to us," while this Perfection of Wisdom is being written out.
Subhūti, when this [perfection] is being pointed out, mastered, recited, properly attended to, and cultivated, this too should be known as a deed of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, Subhūti, Māra the Evil One will approach bodhisattvas in the guise of a monk and speak to them thus:
"If a bodhisattva who practices this profound perfection of wisdom were to realize the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*),

or attain the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, arhatship, or even attain solitary awakening (*pratyekabodhi*)," having heard such words, he will not practice the perfection of wisdom.
Subhūti, this too will be a lack of harmony when this profound perfection of wisdom is being spoken, taught, recited, and even practiced.
"Subhūti, this too should be understood as a work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. Thus is the employment of division by Māra, the Evil One.

Furthermore, Subhūti, while this profound perfection of wisdom is being written down, and so on, up to being cultivated, many works of Māra will arise; those works of Māra which will act as obstacles must be avoided by the bodhisattva mahāsattva."
Subhūti said:
"Blessed One, what are those deeds of Māra that must be understood by a bodhisattva mahāsattva, and having understood them, avoided?
The Blessed One said:

Subhūti, counterfeit forms of the perfection of wisdom— acts of Māra— will arise. Likewise, counterfeit forms of the perfection of meditation, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of patience, the perfection of ethical discipline,
and the perfection of generosity— acts of Māra— will arise, which a bodhisattva mahāsattva must recognize and, having recognized them, avoid.
Furthermore, Subhūti, there will arise deeds of Māra that are counterfeits of internal emptiness, up to and including counterfeits of the emptiness of the essential nature of non-existence;
there will also arise deeds of Māra associated with the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.
Having recognized these, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva should avoid the deeds of Māra, and he shall speak as follows:
Master these; having mastered them, right here attain the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and arhatship.

You should cultivate these very four foundations of mindfulness; cultivate the right efforts; cultivate the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the path;
and cultivate the gateway to liberation that is emptiness, the gateway to liberation that is signlessness, and the gateway to liberation that is wishlessness.
"What need have you to realize unexcelled, perfect enlightenment?
Subhūti, this too will be a lack of harmony when this profound perfection of wisdom is being written down, taken up, and so forth, up to being brought to mind."
While this is being cultivated, Māra the Evil One will bring forth such deeds of Māra. This is the presentation of counterfeits.

Furthermore, Subhūti, Māra the Evil One will approach in the guise of a Buddha, with a body the color of gold and emitting a fathom-wide radiance; when the Bodhisattva sees him there, he will conceive a longing for it and will fall away from omniscience.
Subhūti, this too will be a lack of harmony when this profound perfection of wisdom is being written down, taught, recited, spoken, properly attended to,
and cultivated; Subhūti, this also should be understood as a work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, Subhūti, Māra the Evil One will manifest before those sons of good family and daughters of good family a community of monks headed by the Buddha;
there, that bodhisattva will conceive a longing, thinking: "May I too, in a future time, become such a Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha."
And thus I would lead a community of monks such that I would teach the Dharma exactly as the Tathāgata teaches it;
he will then conceive a longing for that, and having conceived that longing, he will fall away from omniscience.
Subhūti, this too will be a lack of harmony.
Subhūti, when this profound *prajñāpāramitā* is being written down, recited, mastered, spoken, attended to, and cultivated,
this too should be understood as a work of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, Subhūti, Māra the Evil One displays many hundreds of bodhisattvas and many thousands of bodhisattvas.
Those bodhisattvas who will practice the perfection of generosity,

and likewise those who will practice the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom,
will conceive a longing for those beings created by Māra; having conceived that longing, they will fall away from omniscience.
This too, Subhūti, will be a lack of harmony when this profound *prajñāpāramitā* is being written down, recited, studied, properly attended to, and cultivated.
This also, Subhūti, should be understood as a deed of Māra for bodhisattva mahāsattvas. For what reason?
For here, Subhūti, in this profound perfection of wisdom, form does not exist;
feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness do not exist.

Neither the aggregates, nor the elements, nor the sense bases, nor dependent origination, nor the factors of dependent origination exist; neither the perfections, nor the factors conducive to awakening, nor the noble truths, nor the immeasurables, the meditative concentrations, or the formless attainments exist; neither the eight liberations, nor the nine successive meditative attainments, nor emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, or the superknowledges exist;
neither all the emptinesses, nor all the samādhis, nor all the doors of dhāraṇī exist.

Neither the powers of a Tathāgata, nor the grounds of self-confidence, nor the analytical knowledges, nor the unique qualities of a Buddha, nor the gateways to liberation, nor awakening exists; and in that, Subhūti, wherein form does not exist, nor feeling, nor perception, nor mental formations, nor consciousness exists.

There are no aggregates, no elements, no sense bases, no dependent origination, no factors of dependent origination, no perfections, no factors conducive to enlightenment, no noble truths, no immeasurables, meditative absorptions, or formless attainments; no eight liberations, no nine successive meditative attainments, no emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, or superknowledges; and no universal emptiness.

Neither all the samādhis, nor all the doors of dhāraṇī, nor the powers of a Tathāgata, nor the fearlessnesses, nor the analytical knowledges, nor the unique qualities of a Buddha, nor the doors of liberation, nor awakening exists;
where there is no awakening, there neither a Buddha, nor Bodhisattvas, nor Śrāvakas exist. For what reason is that?
"Subhūti, all dharmas are indeed empty of intrinsic nature.
Thus, there arises a longing for objects that are not as they appear;
furthermore, Subhūti, this perfection of wisdom will have many obstacles.

For those sons of good family and daughters of good family who uphold, recite, explain, study, and correctly attend to this perfection of wisdom— Subhūti, it is just as if, for example, the jewels of Jambudvīpa,
namely gold, gems, pearls, beryl, conch shells, crystals, coral, silver, and so forth, were subject to many obstacles and many adversaries.

They will come to pass. It is even so, Subhūti: for those sons of good family and daughters of good family who write down this profound perfection of wisdom, teach it, master it, recite it, speak it, attend to it with wise reflection, and cultivate it, many obstacles will arise.
"There are many adversaries.
Subhūti said: "So it is, Blessed One; so it is, Sugata."
Sūtras associated with the perfection of wisdom will face many adversaries.

Those deluded persons, possessed by Māra, will create obstacles for those who write down, teach, recite, and cultivate this profound perfection of wisdom. Blessed One, those deluded persons will be of little intelligence.
Those of dull intellect who will create obstacles while this profound *prajñāpāramitā* is being written, up to being cultivated—they shall not possess the most sublime of dharmas.

Those who will not write down this profound *prajñāpāramitā*, who will create obstacles while it is being written, and so on, up to those who will not cultivate it, and who will create obstacles while it is being cultivated.
The Blessed One said:
"So it is, Subhūti; so it is. Those sons of good family and daughters of good family will be possessed by Māra;

they will have newly set out in the vehicle, will not have planted roots of merit, will have meager roots of merit, will not have performed services for previous Victors, and will not be sustained by spiritual friends."
